name: e_neg
doc: /-- `e (−θ) = cos θ − i sin θ`. -/
sig: theorem e_neg (θ : ℝ) : e (-θ) = (Real.cos θ : ℂ) - (Real.sin θ : ℂ) * I

name: e_ne_zero
doc: /-- `e θ` is never zero (it has norm `1`). -/
sig: theorem e_ne_zero (θ : ℝ) : e θ ≠ 0

name: norm_sq_neg_one_add_e_add_e
doc: /-- Squared norm of `−1 + e u + e v`, in coordinates. -/
sig: theorem norm_sq_neg_one_add_e_add_e (u v : ℝ) : ‖(-1 : ℂ) + e u + e v‖ ^ 2 = (-1 + Real.cos u + Real.cos v) ^ 2 + (Real.sin u + Real.sin v) ^ 2

name: twoCirc_diff
doc: /-- The difference of the two turned points is `(y₁ − y₀)(−1 + e(σ s) + e(−σ t))`. -/
sig: theorem twoCirc_diff (y₀ y₁ : ℂ) (u v : ℝ) : (y₀ + (y₁ - y₀) * e u) - (y₁ + (y₀ - y₁) * e v) = (y₁ - y₀) * ((-1 : ℂ) + e u + e v)

name: ringPt_sub_ringPt
doc: /-- The chord of a unit circle as a vector: `r(β) − r(α) = 2 sin((β − α)/2) · e((α + β)/2 + π/2)`. -/
sig: theorem ringPt_sub_ringPt (p : ℂ) (α β : ℝ) : ringPt p β - ringPt p α = ((2 * Real.sin ((β - α) / 2) : ℝ) : ℂ) * e ((α + β) / 2 + π / 2)

name: dist_ringPt_ringPt
doc:
/-- **FS116-V4-CHORD**, distance: two points of a unit circle at angular separation `δ = |α − β| ∈ [0, π]` are at
distance `2 sin(δ/2)`. -/
sig: theorem dist_ringPt_ringPt (p : ℂ) {α β : ℝ} (hδ : |α - β| ≤ π) : dist (ringPt p α) (ringPt p β) = 2 * Real.sin (|α - β| / 2)

name: norm_e_sub_e_le
doc: /-- Unit vectors are `1`-Lipschitz in the angle: `|e θ − e θ₀| ≤ |θ − θ₀|`. -/
sig: theorem norm_e_sub_e_le (θ θ₀ : ℝ) : ‖e θ - e θ₀‖ ≤ |θ - θ₀|

name: dist_ringPt_ringPt_cmp_one
doc:
/-- **FS116-V4-CHORD**, the three regimes: at separation `δ ∈ [0, π]` the distance is `1` exactly at `δ = π/3`, below
`1` for `δ < π/3`, above `1` for `π/3 < δ`. -/
sig: theorem dist_ringPt_ringPt_cmp_one (p : ℂ) {α β : ℝ} (hδ : |α - β| ≤ π) : (dist (ringPt p α) (ringPt p β) = 1 ↔ |α - β| = π / 3) ∧ (dist (ringPt p α) (ringPt p β) < 1 ↔ |α - β| < π / 3) ∧ (1 < dist (ringPt p α) (ringPt p β) ↔ π / 3 < |α - β|)

name: twoCirc_identity
doc:
/-- **FS129-SR1-TWOCIRC**: let `|y₀ − y₁| = 1` and let `p = y₀ + (y₁ − y₀) e(σπ/3)` (`σ = ±1`: `p` is the third vertex
of a unit equilateral triangle on `y₀y₁`, and `σ` is the turning sense "toward `p`"); put
`a(s) = y₀ + (y₁ − y₀) e(σ s)` (from `y₁`, turning `s` about `y₀` toward `p`) and `b(t) = y₁ + (y₀ − y₁) e(−σ t)`
(from `y₀`, turning `t` about `y₁` toward `p`). Then
`|a(s) − b(t)|² − 1 = −8
sig: theorem twoCirc_identity {y₀ y₁ : ℂ} (h01 : dist y₀ y₁ = 1) {σ : ℝ} (hσ : σ = 1 ∨ σ = -1) (s t : ℝ) : ‖(y₀ + (y₁ - y₀) * e (σ * s)) - (y₁ + (y₀ - y₁) * e (-(σ * t)))‖ ^ 2 - 1 = -8 * Real.sin (s / 2) * Real.sin (t / 2) * Real.cos ((s + t) / 2) ∧ ‖(y₀ + (y₁ - y₀) * e (σ * s)) - (y₁ + (y₀ - y₁) * e (-(σ * t)))‖ ^ 2 - 1 = 2 * (1 - Real.cos s) * (1 - Real.cos t) - 2 * Real.sin s * Real.sin t

name: twoCirc_cmp_one
doc:
/-- **FS129-SR1-TWOCIRC**, the regimes: for `0 < s, t < π`, `|a(s) − b(t)|` is below `1` when `s + t < π`, equal to `1`
when `s + t = π`, above `1` when `s + t > π`. -/
sig: theorem twoCirc_cmp_one {y₀ y₁ : ℂ} (h01 : dist y₀ y₁ = 1) {σ : ℝ} (hσ : σ = 1 ∨ σ = -1) {s t : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) (hs' : s < π) (ht : 0 < t) (ht' : t < π) : (s + t < π → dist (y₀ + (y₁ - y₀) * e (σ * s)) (y₁ + (y₀ - y₁) * e (-(σ * t))) < 1) ∧ (s + t = π → dist (y₀ + (y₁ - y₀) * e (σ * s)) (y₁ + (y₀ - y₁) * e (-(σ * t))) = 1) ∧ (π < s + t → 1 < dist (y₀ + (y₁ - y₀) * e (σ * s)) (y₁ + (y₀ - y₁) * e (-(σ * t))))

name: exists_sign_of_equilateral
doc:
/-- The row's hypothesis read back: every `p` with `|p − y₀| = |p − y₁| = 1 = |y₀ − y₁|` is `y₀ + (y₁ − y₀) e(σπ/3)`
for one of `σ = ±1`, so `twoCirc_identity` covers every configuration the row names. -/
sig: theorem exists_sign_of_equilateral {y₀ y₁ p : ℂ} (h01 : dist y₀ y₁ = 1) (hp0 : dist p y₀ = 1) (hp1 : dist p y₁ = 1) : ∃ σ : ℝ, (σ = 1 ∨ σ = -1) ∧ p = y₀ + (y₁ - y₀) * e (σ * (π / 3))

name: xcorner
doc:
/-- **FS121-D1-XCORNER**: at a convex corner `z` of angle `θ ∈ (0, π)` with straight edges along `e(φ)` and
`e(φ + θ)`, the inner unit parallels of the two edges (`z + s e(φ) + e(φ + π/2)` and `z + t e(φ + θ) + e(φ + θ − π/2)`)
meet exactly when `s = t = cot(θ/2)`, at the point at distance `1/sin(θ/2)` from `z` on the bisector. -/
sig: theorem xcorner {θ : ℝ} (hθ : 0 < θ) (hθ' : θ < π) (z : ℂ) (φ : ℝ) (s t : ℝ) : (z + s * e φ + e (φ + π / 2) = z + t * e (φ + θ) + e (φ + θ - π / 2) ↔ s = Real.cot (θ / 2) ∧ t = Real.cot (θ / 2)) ∧ z + (Real.cot (θ / 2) : ℂ) * e φ + e (φ + π / 2) = z + ((1 / Real.sin (θ / 2) : ℝ) : ℂ) * e (φ + θ / 2)

name: lens_stepA
doc:
/-- Step A of EXIT's core: a unit vector `d` (the exit point relative to `e b`, in the frame of `e b`) lying in the lens (so
within `1` of the other centre, `n' = (1 − C, S)`) lies strictly left of the direction `e(120°)`. -/

name: lens_stepB
doc:
/-- Step B of EXIT's core: with `d` strictly left of `e(120°)`, a unit `n` turned counter-clockwise from `d` (by at most
`180°`) with `d + n` within `1` of `e(120°)` is `−d`. -/

name: lens_core
doc:
/-- **The core of EXIT, one circle.** At a point `x` of `ω(e b)` inside `B̄(e a, 1)` (`30° < b < 90°`, `−90° < a < −30°`), a unit
vector `ν` turned counter-clockwise from `x − e b` (by at most `180°`) whose tip `x + ν` lies within `1` of `e(b + 60°)` is
`e b − x`. -/
sig: theorem lens_core {a b : ℝ} (hb₁ : π / 6 < b) (hb₂ : b < π / 2) (ha₁ : -(π / 2) < a) (ha₂ : a < -(π / 6)) {x ν : ℂ} (hν : ‖ν‖ = 1) (hxb : ‖x - e b‖ = 1) (hxa : ‖x - e a‖ ≤ 1) (hcr : 0 ≤ (ν * (starRingEnd ℂ) (x - e b)).im) (hP : ‖x + ν - e (b + π / 3)‖ ≤ 1) : x + ν = e b

name: deriv_nonneg_of_leftmax
doc: /-- A real function with a left derivative `g'` at `te` and `g t ≤ g te` just before `te` has `0 ≤ g'`. -/
sig: theorem deriv_nonneg_of_leftmax {g : ℝ → ℝ} {g' te : ℝ} (h : HasDerivWithinAt g g' (Iic te) te) (hle : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[<] te, g t ≤ g te) : 0 ≤ g'

name: re_conj_mul_nonneg_of_exit
doc: /-- A curve inside `B(c, 1)` just before `te` and on `ω(c)` at `te` leaves outward: `0 ≤ Re (conj (γ te − c) γ')`. -/
sig: theorem re_conj_mul_nonneg_of_exit {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {γ' c : ℂ} {te : ℝ} (hγ : HasDerivWithinAt γ γ' (Iic te) te) (hin : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[<] te, ‖γ t - c‖ < 1) (hxc : ‖γ te - c‖ = 1) : 0 ≤ ((starRingEnd ℂ) (γ te - c) * γ').re

name: im_leftNormal_mul_conj
doc: /-- `Im (ν conj d) = Re (conj d γ') / ‖γ'‖` for the left normal `ν = i γ'/‖γ'‖`. -/
sig: theorem im_leftNormal_mul_conj {γ' d : ℂ} (hγ' : γ' ≠ 0) : (leftNormal γ' * (starRingEnd ℂ) d).im = ((starRingEnd ℂ) d * γ').re / ‖γ'‖

name: exit_lens
doc:
/-- **FS116-S1-EXIT** at the class its argument reads: with `30° < b < 90°`, `−90° < a < −30°`, a curve with left derivative
`γ' ≠ 0` at `t_e`, inside `Λ` just before `t_e` and on its frontier at `t_e` other than `0`, whose left unit normal `ν` at
`t_e` meets the four distance conditions, exits with `γ(t_e) + ν = e(b)` or `γ(t_e) − ν = e(a)`. -/
sig: theorem exit_lens {a b : ℝ} (hb₁ : π / 6 < b) (hb₂ : b < π / 2) (ha₁ : -(π / 2) < a) (ha₂ : a < -(π / 6)) {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {γ' : ℂ} {te : ℝ} (hγ : HasDerivWithinAt γ γ' (Iic te) te) (hγ' : γ' ≠ 0) (hin : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[<] te, γ t ∈ lensΛ a b) (hexit : γ te ∈ frontier (lensΛ a b)) (hne : γ te ≠ 0) (h3 : dist (γ te + leftNormal γ') (e (b + π / 3)) ≤ 1) (h5 : dist (γ te - leftNormal γ') (e (a - π / 3)) ≤ 1) (h3' : 1 ≤ dist (γ te) (e (b + π / 3))) (h5' : 1 ≤ dist (γ te) (e (a - π / 3))) : γ te + leftNormal γ' = e b ∨ γ te - leftNormal γ' = e a

name: exit_lens_row
doc:
/-- **FS116-S1-EXIT**, the row's form: a `C¹` curve on `[0, t_e]` with nonvanishing velocity, `γ(0) = 0`, `γ(t) ∈ Λ` for
`0 < t < t_e` and `γ(t_e) ∈ ∂Λ \ {0}`, meeting the four conditions at `t_e` with its left unit normal, exits with
`γ(t_e) + ν(t_e) = y_b` or `γ(t_e) − ν(t_e) = y_a`. -/
sig: theorem exit_lens_row {a b : ℝ} (hb₁ : π / 6 < b) (hb₂ : b < π / 2) (ha₁ : -(π / 2) < a) (ha₂ : a < -(π / 6)) {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {te : ℝ} (hte : 0 < te) (hC1 : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (Icc 0 te)) (hreg : ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 te, derivWithin γ (Icc 0 te) t ≠ 0) (h0 : γ 0 = 0) (hin : ∀ t ∈ Ioo 0 te, γ t ∈ lensΛ a b) (hexit : γ te ∈ frontier (lensΛ a b)) (hne : γ te ≠ 0) (h3 : dist (γ te + leftNormal (derivWithin γ (Icc 0 te) te)) (e (b + π / 3)) ≤ 1) (h5 : dist (γ te - leftNormal (derivWithin γ (Icc 0 te) te)) (e (a - π / 3)) ≤ 1) (h3' : 1 ≤ dist (γ te) (e (b + π / 3))) (h5' : 1 ≤ dist (γ te) (e (a - π / 3))) : γ te + leftNormal (derivWithin γ (Icc 0 te) te) = e b ∨ γ te - leftNormal (derivWithin γ (Icc 0 te) te) = e a

doc: /-- The carrier of the arc `circ p 1 θ₀ θ₁` is the closed sub-arc `r([θ₀, θ₁])` of `ω(p)`. -/
sig: theorem carrier_circ_unit (p : ℂ) (θ₀ θ₁ : ℝ) : (Arc.circ p 1 θ₀ θ₁).carrier = ringArc p θ₀ θ₁

name: Arc.OnRing
doc: /-- `a` is an arc of the unit circle `ω(p)`. -/
sig: def Arc.OnRing (p : ℂ) (a : Arc) : Prop

name: Arc.OnRing.carrier_subset_sphere
doc: /-- An arc on `ω(p)` has its carrier on `ω(p)`. -/
sig: theorem Arc.OnRing.carrier_subset_sphere {p : ℂ} {a : Arc} (h : a.OnRing p) : a.carrier ⊆ sphere p 1

name: polarPt
doc: /-- The polar point `p + ρ e(ψ)`. -/
sig: noncomputable def polarPt (p : ℂ) (ρ ψ : ℝ) : ℂ

name: continuous_polarPt
doc: /-- The polar map is continuous. -/
sig: theorem continuous_polarPt (p : ℂ) : Continuous (fun q : ℝ × ℝ => polarPt p q.1 q.2)

name: norm_polarPt_sub
doc: /-- The distance from the centre of a polar point is `|ρ|`. -/
sig: theorem norm_polarPt_sub (p : ℂ) (ρ ψ : ℝ) : ‖polarPt p ρ ψ - p‖ = |ρ|

name: dist_polarPt_ringPt_le
doc: /-- A polar point at radius within `ε` of `1` and angle within `κ` of `φ` is within `ε + κ` of `r(φ)`. -/
sig: theorem dist_polarPt_ringPt_le (p : ℂ) (ρ ψ φ : ℝ) : dist (polarPt p ρ ψ) (ringPt p φ) ≤ |ρ - 1| + |ψ - φ|

name: abs_norm_sub_one_le
sig: theorem abs_norm_sub_one_le (p z : ℂ) (φ : ℝ) : |‖z - p‖ - 1| ≤ dist z (ringPt p φ)

name: polar_nbhd
doc:
/-- **Polar neighbourhoods**: every point `z` near `r(φ)` is `p + ρ e(ψ)` with `ρ = ‖z − p‖` near `1` and `ψ` in a given open
interval about `φ`. -/
sig: theorem polar_nbhd (p : ℂ) {φ α β : ℝ} (h : φ ∈ Ioo α β) : ∃ ν > 0, ∀ z : ℂ, dist z (ringPt p φ) < ν → |‖z - p‖ - 1| < ν ∧ ∃ ψ ∈ Ioo α β, z = polarPt p ‖z - p‖ ψ

name: e_eq_e_iff
doc: /-- `e a = e b` exactly when `a − b` is an integer multiple of `2π`. -/
sig: theorem e_eq_e_iff {a b : ℝ} : e a = e b ↔ ∃ n : ℤ, a = b + n * (2 * π)

name: exists_mem_Icc_e_eq
doc: /-- Every angle is congruent mod `2π` to one in `[θ₀, θ₀ + 2π]`. -/
sig: theorem exists_mem_Icc_e_eq (θ₀ x : ℝ) : ∃ ψ ∈ Icc θ₀ (θ₀ + 2 * π), e ψ = e x

name: e_ne_one
sig: theorem e_ne_one {t : ℝ} (h0 : t ≠ 0) (h1 : |t| < 2 * π) : e t ≠ 1

name: dist_ringPt_side_le
doc: /-- A ring point `t ≥ 0` along a side of `r(θ)` is within `t` of it. -/
sig: theorem dist_ringPt_side_le (p : ℂ) (θ : ℝ) (s : Side) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) : dist (ringPt p (θ + s.sign * t)) (ringPt p θ) ≤ t

name: dist_lt_of_mem_germ
doc: /-- A point of the germ of `ω(p)` of length `δ` is within `δ` of the base point. -/
sig: theorem dist_lt_of_mem_germ {p : ℂ} {θ : ℝ} {s : Side} {δ : ℝ} {x : ℂ} (h : x ∈ germ p θ s δ) : dist x (ringPt p θ) < δ

name: ringPt_notMem_germ
doc: /-- The base point of a germ of length below `2π` is not on it. -/
sig: theorem ringPt_notMem_germ {p : ℂ} {θ : ℝ} {s : Side} {δ : ℝ} (hδ : δ ≤ 2 * π) : ringPt p θ ∉ germ p θ s δ

name: isPreconnected_germ
doc: /-- The germ is preconnected. -/
sig: theorem isPreconnected_germ (p : ℂ) (θ : ℝ) (s : Side) (δ : ℝ) : IsPreconnected (germ p θ s δ)

name: sideInterval
doc:
/-- The angles of the closed (open) sub-arc of the germ's side of `θ` of length `δ` are `θ + sign · u` for `u ∈ [0, δ]`
(`(0, δ)`). -/
sig: theorem sideInterval (θ δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) (s : Side) : θ < θ + δ ∧ (s = .ccw → ∀ φ, (φ ∈ Icc θ (θ + δ) ↔ ∃ u ∈ Icc 0 δ, φ = θ + s.sign * u)) ∧ (s = .cw → ∀ φ, (φ ∈ Icc (θ - δ) θ ↔ ∃ u ∈ Icc 0 δ, φ = θ + s.sign * u))

name: exists_germ_subset_ringArc
doc:
/-- **A germ that an arc of `ω(p)` meets arbitrarily close to its base point lies in it** (for short germs): `r(θ)` lies on
the arc `r([θ₀, θ₁])` and every germ of length `δ` meets it. -/
sig: theorem exists_germ_subset_ringArc {p : ℂ} {θ θ₀ θ₁ : ℝ} (hlt : θ₀ < θ₁) (hle : θ₁ ≤ θ₀ + 2 * π) (s : Side) (hy : ringPt p θ ∈ ringArc p θ₀ θ₁) (hhit : ∀ δ > 0, (germ p θ s δ ∩ ringArc p θ₀ θ₁).Nonempty) {δ₀ : ℝ} (hδ₀ : 0 < δ₀) : ∃ δ' > 0, δ' ≤ δ₀ ∧ germ p θ s δ' ⊆ ringArc p θ₀ θ₁

name: coneAt_biUnion_finite
doc: /-- The cone of a finite union is the union of the cones. -/
sig: theorem coneAt_biUnion_finite {ι : Type*} {s : Set ι} (hs : s.Finite) (T : ι → Set ℂ) {y : ℂ} {β : ℝ} (h : β ∈ coneAt (⋃ i ∈ s, T i) y) : ∃ i ∈ s, β ∈ coneAt (T i) y

name: coneAt_inter_ball
doc: /-- The cone at `y` is local: it sees only a ball about `y`. -/
sig: theorem coneAt_inter_ball {S : Set ℂ} {y : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {β : ℝ} (h : β ∈ coneAt S y) : β ∈ coneAt (S ∩ ball y r) y

name: curveAt
doc:
/-- The full curve through `x` with data `(κ, b)`: `κ = 0` the line through `x` normal to `b`, `κ = 1` the circle through
`x` centred at `x + b`. -/
sig: def curveAt (x : ℂ) (κ : ℝ) (b : ℂ) : Set ℂ

name: mem_curveAt_scale
doc: /-- A point scaled away from `x` along the ray through `w` stays off the curve, if `w` lies outside it (or off the line). -/
sig: theorem mem_curveAt_scale {x : ℂ} {κ : ℝ} {b w : ℂ} (hout : (κ = 0 ∧ ((w - x) * (starRingEnd ℂ) b).re ≠ 0) ∨ (κ = 1 ∧ 2 * ((w - x) * (starRingEnd ℂ) b).re < Complex.normSq (w - x))) {t : ℝ} (ht : 1 ≤ t) : x + (t : ℂ) * (w - x) ∉ curveAt x κ b

name: farther_out
doc: /-- The outward case of `exists_farther`: from a point outside the circle (or off the line) go radially away from `x`. -/
sig: theorem farther_out {x z : ℂ} {κ : ℝ} {b w : ℂ} (hout : (κ = 0 ∧ ((w - x) * (starRingEnd ℂ) b).re ≠ 0) ∨ (κ = 1 ∧ 2 * ((w - x) * (starRingEnd ℂ) b).re < Complex.normSq (w - x))) {δ : ℝ} (hδ0 : 0 < δ) (hδ : δ ≤ ‖z - x‖) (hw : dist w z < δ / 3) : ∃ w' : ℂ, ‖z - x‖ < ‖w' - x‖ ∧ segment ℝ w w' ⊆ ball z δ ∧ Disjoint (segment ℝ w w') (curveAt x κ b)

name: circle_step_real
doc: /-- The two coordinate identities of the inward step of `farther_in`. -/

name: farther_in
doc: /-- The inward case of `exists_farther`: from a point inside the circle step into the disc along `(β − s) p + s b`, a direction that enters the disc and leaves the circle about `x`. -/
sig: theorem farther_in {x z b w : ℂ} (hb : b ≠ 0) (hz : z ∈ curveAt x 1 b) (hd : 0 < ‖z - x‖) (hbig : ‖z - x‖ < 2 * ‖b‖) {δ : ℝ} (hδ0 : 0 < δ) (hw : dist w z < δ) (hin : Complex.normSq (w - x) < 2 * ((w - x) * (starRingEnd ℂ) b).re) : ∃ w' : ℂ, ‖z - x‖ < ‖w' - x‖ ∧ segment ℝ w w' ⊆ ball z δ ∧ Disjoint (segment ℝ w w') (curveAt x 1 b)

name: exists_farther
doc:
/-- **Farther points beside a curve** (the farthest-point lemma's local step): near a point `z ≠ x` of a curve through `x`
(a line, or a circle of diameter above `‖z − x‖`), every point `w` off the curve is joined, by a segment off the curve and
inside `B(z, δ)`, to a point strictly farther from `x` than `z`. -/
sig: theorem exists_farther {x z : ℂ} {κ : ℝ} (hκ : κ = 0 ∨ κ = 1) {b : ℂ} (hb : b ≠ 0) (hz : z ∈ curveAt x κ b) (hd : 0 < ‖z - x‖) (hbig : κ = 1 → ‖z - x‖ < 2 * ‖b‖) {δ : ℝ} (hδ0 : 0 < δ) (hδ : δ ≤ ‖z - x‖) {w : ℂ} (hw : dist w z < δ / 3) (hwc : w ∉ curveAt x κ b) : ∃ w' : ℂ, ‖z - x‖ < ‖w' - x‖ ∧ segment ℝ w w' ⊆ ball z δ ∧ Disjoint (segment ℝ w w') (curveAt x κ b)

name: re_mul_conj_eq
doc: /-- `Re (m · conj b)` in coordinates. -/
sig: theorem re_mul_conj_eq (m b : ℂ) : (m * (starRingEnd ℂ) b).re = m.re * b.re + m.im * b.im

name: sq_re_im_ne
doc: /-- A nonzero complex number has nonzero squared coordinates sum. -/
sig: theorem sq_re_im_ne {b : ℂ} (hb : b ≠ 0) : b.re ^ 2 + b.im ^ 2 ≠ 0

name: eq_of_re_im
doc: /-- A complex number with zero coordinates is `0`. -/
sig: theorem eq_of_re_im {m : ℂ} (h1 : m.re = 0) (h2 : m.im = 0) : m = 0

name: perp_circle
doc: /-- A vector `m` perpendicular to `d` on the circle `|m|² = 2 m·b` is `0` or has `|m|²|d|² = 4 (d × b)²`. -/

name: curve_inter
doc: /-- Two distinct full curves through `x` meet near `x` only at `x`. -/
sig: theorem curve_inter {x : ℂ} {κ κ' : ℝ} (hκ : κ = 0 ∨ κ = 1) (hκ' : κ' = 0 ∨ κ' = 1) {b b' : ℂ} (hb : b ≠ 0) (hb' : b' ≠ 0) (hsame : ¬ (κ = κ' ∧ (κ = 1 → b = b') ∧ (κ = 0 → (b * (starRingEnd ℂ) b').im = 0))) : ∃ ε > 0, ∀ z : ℂ, ‖z - x‖ < ε → z ∈ curveAt x κ b → z ∈ curveAt x κ' b' → z = x

name: curveAt_eq_of_same
doc: /-- Curves with the same data (a circle with its centre; parallel lines) coincide. -/
sig: theorem curveAt_eq_of_same {x : ℂ} {κ κ' : ℝ} (hκ : κ = 0 ∨ κ = 1) {b b' : ℂ} (hb : b ≠ 0) (hb' : b' ≠ 0) (hsame : κ = κ' ∧ (κ = 1 → b = b') ∧ (κ = 0 → (b * (starRingEnd ℂ) b').im = 0)) : curveAt x κ b = curveAt x κ' b'

name: Arc.curveData
doc:
/-- The data `(κ, b)` of the full curve carrying an arc through `x`: the line through `x` along a segment, the circle through
`x` about the centre of a circular arc. -/
sig: noncomputable def Arc.curveData (x : ℂ) : Arc → ℝ × ℂ | .seg u v => (0, I * (v - u)) | .circ c _ _ _ => (1, c - x)

name: Arc.curve
doc: /-- The full curve through `x` carrying an arc. -/
sig: def Arc.curve (x : ℂ) (a : Arc) : Set ℂ

name: Arc.curveData_kappa
doc: /-- The `κ` of an arc's curve data is `0` or `1`. -/
sig: theorem Arc.curveData_kappa (x : ℂ) (a : Arc) : (a.curveData x).1 = 0 ∨ (a.curveData x).1 = 1

name: Arc.curveData_ne
doc: /-- The vector of an arc's curve data is nonzero for a nondegenerate arc through `x`. -/
sig: theorem Arc.curveData_ne {x : ℂ} {a : Arc} (ha : a.Nondegenerate) (hx : x ∈ a.carrier) : (a.curveData x).2 ≠ 0

name: Arc.carrier_subset_curve
doc: /-- An arc through `x` lies on its full curve through `x`. -/
sig: theorem Arc.carrier_subset_curve {x : ℂ} {a : Arc} (hx : x ∈ a.carrier) : a.carrier ⊆ a.curve x

name: exists_notMem_curveAt
doc: /-- An open nonempty set has a point off any curve. -/
sig: theorem exists_notMem_curveAt {x : ℂ} {κ : ℝ} (hκ : κ = 0 ∨ κ = 1) {b : ℂ} (hb : b ≠ 0) {O : Set ℂ} (hO : IsOpen O) (hne : O.Nonempty) : ∃ w ∈ O, w ∉ curveAt x κ b

name: finite_perp_circle
doc: /-- The points `m` of a circle about `0` with fixed inner product against `b ≠ 0` are finitely many (at most two). -/
sig: theorem finite_perp_circle (b : ℂ) (hb : b ≠ 0) (c K : ℝ) : {m : ℂ | m.re * b.re + m.im * b.im = c ∧ m.re ^ 2 + m.im ^ 2 = K}.Finite

name: finite_curve_inter_sphere
doc: /-- A curve through `x` meets a circle about `x` in finitely many points. -/
sig: theorem finite_curve_inter_sphere {x : ℂ} {κ : ℝ} {b : ℂ} (hb : b ≠ 0) (ρ : ℝ) : (curveAt x κ b ∩ sphere x ρ).Finite

name: finite_image_of_locConst
doc: /-- A function on an interval that is locally constant off a finite set takes finitely many values off it. -/
sig: theorem finite_image_of_locConst {β : Type*} (g : ℝ → β) {Θ : Set ℝ} (hΘ : Θ.Finite) : ∀ {a b : ℝ}, (∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, t ∉ Θ → ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝 t, g s = g t) → (g '' (Ioo a b \ Θ)).Finite

name: covers_one_iff
doc:
/-- A fragment covers `B̄(p, 1)` exactly when it covers a closed disc of radius above `1` about `p`: the domain is open and
the disc compact. Every row's "on a closed disc of radius above 1 about `p`" is stated as `F.Covers p 1`. -/
sig: theorem covers_one_iff (p : ℂ) : F.Covers p 1 ↔ ∃ R, 1 < R ∧ F.Covers p R

name: finite_ringΓ_off_ringArc
doc:
/-- On a covered ring, the points of `Γ` that lie on no arc of `Γ` on `ω(p)` are finitely many: the ring is compact, each
of its points has a neighbourhood meeting finitely many arcs, and each arc not on `ω(p)` meets `ω(p)` in finitely many
points (`Arc.finite_inter_sphere_or_eq_circ`). -/
sig: theorem finite_ringΓ_off_ringArc {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) : ((F.Γ ∩ sphere p 1) \ {x | F.OnRingArc p x}).Finite

name: dense_interiorPts
doc: /-- `Γ` has empty interior: every point of the domain is a limit of interior points. -/
sig: theorem dense_interiorPts : F.dom ⊆ closure F.interiorPts

name: exists_mem_coloursAt
doc: /-- Every point of the domain carries a colour. -/
sig: theorem exists_mem_coloursAt {x : ℂ} (hx : x ∈ F.dom) : ∃ c, c ∈ F.coloursAt x

name: finite_ray_inter_sphere
doc: /-- A line meets a circle in finitely many points: `{s | ‖x + s w − c‖ = ρ}` is finite when `w ≠ 0`. -/
sig: theorem finite_ray_inter_sphere (x c w : ℂ) (ρ : ℝ) (hw : w ≠ 0) : {s : ℝ | ‖x + (s : ℂ) * w - c‖ = ρ}.Finite

name: subsingleton_ray_inter_segment
doc: /-- A ray `x + s w` with `w` not parallel to the segment `[u, v]` meets it in at most one point. -/
sig: theorem subsingleton_ray_inter_segment (x u v w : ℂ) (hd : v - u ≠ 0) (hpar : (w * (starRingEnd ℂ) (v - u)).im ≠ 0) : {s : ℝ | x + (s : ℂ) * w ∈ segment ℝ u v}.Subsingleton

name: exists_ray_in_interiorPts
doc:
/-- **A ray from a point of the domain** (child of engine 2): there are a direction `w ≠ 0` and `ε > 0` with
`x + s w` an interior point for all `0 < s < ε`. -/
sig: theorem exists_ray_in_interiorPts {x : ℂ} (hx : x ∈ F.dom) : ∃ w : ℂ, w ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ ε > 0, ∀ s ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) ε, x + (s : ℂ) * w ∈ F.interiorPts

name: mem_closure_tile
doc:
/-- **Engine 2.** Every point of the domain lies in the closure of some tile: a ray from it into the interior points
is connected, so lies in one tile. -/
sig: theorem mem_closure_tile {x : ℂ} (hx : x ∈ F.dom) : ∃ T, F.IsTile T ∧ x ∈ closure T

name: exists_ball_finite
doc: /-- Near a point of the domain, a ball in the domain meets only finitely many arcs. -/
sig: theorem exists_ball_finite {y : ℂ} (hy : y ∈ F.dom) : ∃ ε > 0, ball y ε ⊆ F.dom ∧ {a | a ∈ F.arcs ∧ (a.carrier ∩ ball y ε).Nonempty}.Finite

name: GoodAt
doc:
/-- `ρ₀` is a **good radius** about `x`: the ball lies in the domain, only finitely many arcs meet it, all pass through `x`,
every circle among them has diameter above `ρ₀`, and distinct full curves through `x` of two of them meet inside the ball
only at `x`. -/
sig: structure GoodAt (x : ℂ) (ρ₀ : ℝ) : Prop

name: exists_goodAt
doc: /-- Every point of the domain has a good radius. -/
sig: theorem exists_goodAt {x : ℂ} (hx : x ∈ F.dom) : ∃ ρ₀, F.GoodAt x ρ₀

name: IsTile.subset_of_preconnected
doc: /-- A preconnected set of interior points meeting a tile lies in it. -/
sig: theorem IsTile.subset_of_preconnected {T : Set ℂ} (hT : F.IsTile T) {s : Set ℂ} (hs : IsPreconnected s) (hsI : s ⊆ F.interiorPts) {t : ℂ} (ht : t ∈ s) (htT : t ∈ T) : s ⊆ T

name: GoodAt.exists_local_curve
doc: /-- Near a point `z ≠ x` of an arc, inside a good ball, every arc point lies on the full curve of that arc. -/
sig: theorem GoodAt.exists_local_curve {x : ℂ} {ρ₀ : ℝ} (hG : F.GoodAt x ρ₀) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ ball x ρ₀) (hzx : z ≠ x) {a : Arc} (ha : a ∈ F.arcs) (hza : z ∈ a.carrier) : ∃ δ > 0, ball z δ ⊆ ball x ρ₀ ∧ ∀ y ∈ ball z δ, ∀ a' ∈ F.arcs, y ∈ a'.carrier → y ∈ a.curve x

name: GoodAt.not_tile_subset_ball
doc:
/-- **No tile lies inside a good ball**: a tile inside `B(x, ρ)`, `ρ < ρ₀`, would have a farthest point `z` of its closure
from `x`; off `Γ` the tile continues beyond `z`, and on `Γ` it lies beside the one curve through `z`, which it cannot
cross, yet which leads outward. -/
sig: theorem GoodAt.not_tile_subset_ball {x : ℂ} {ρ₀ : ℝ} (hG : F.GoodAt x ρ₀) {T : Set ℂ} (hT : F.IsTile T) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : ρ < ρ₀) (hsub : T ⊆ ball x ρ) : False

name: spherePt
doc: /-- The point of the circle `S(x, ρ)` at angle `θ`. -/
sig: noncomputable def spherePt (x : ℂ) (ρ θ : ℝ) : ℂ

name: continuous_spherePt
doc: /-- `θ ↦ spherePt x ρ θ` is continuous. -/
sig: theorem continuous_spherePt (x : ℂ) (ρ : ℝ) : Continuous (spherePt x ρ)

name: norm_spherePt_sub
doc: /-- `spherePt x ρ θ` is at distance `ρ` from `x`. -/
sig: theorem norm_spherePt_sub (x : ℂ) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ) (θ : ℝ) : ‖spherePt x ρ θ - x‖ = ρ

name: spherePt_mem_sphere
doc: /-- `spherePt x ρ θ` lies on `S(x, ρ)`. -/
sig: theorem spherePt_mem_sphere (x : ℂ) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ) (θ : ℝ) : spherePt x ρ θ ∈ sphere x ρ

name: injOn_spherePt
doc: /-- `spherePt x ρ` is injective on an interval of length `2π`. -/
sig: theorem injOn_spherePt (x : ℂ) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (a : ℝ) : InjOn (spherePt x ρ) (Ioo a (a + 2 * π))

name: GoodAt.finite_tiles_sphere
doc:
/-- **Finitely many tiles meet a small circle**: off the finitely many points of `Γ` on it, the circle's points fall into
finitely many arcs, each inside one tile. -/
sig: theorem GoodAt.finite_tiles_sphere {x : ℂ} {ρ₀ : ℝ} (hG : F.GoodAt x ρ₀) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ0 : 0 < ρ) (hρ : ρ < ρ₀) : {T | F.IsTile T ∧ (T ∩ sphere x ρ).Nonempty}.Finite

name: region_inter_ball_subset
doc: /-- The tiles of colour `c` meeting a small ball cover the colour class inside it. -/
sig: theorem region_inter_ball_subset {x : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (c : Fin k) : F.region c ∩ ball x r ⊆ ⋃ T ∈ {T | F.TileOf c T ∧ (T ∩ ball x r).Nonempty}, T

name: finite_tiles_near
doc:
/-- **Finitely many tiles meet a small disc about any point of the domain**: near `x` only the arcs through `x` remain,
every pair of their full curves meets only at `x`, and every tile meeting `B(x, r)` meets a fixed small circle about `x`
(a tile inside the ball would have a farthest point, `GoodAt.not_tile_subset_ball`); only finitely many tiles meet that
circle (`GoodAt.finite_tiles_sphere`).
sig: theorem finite_tiles_near {x : ℂ} (hx : x ∈ F.dom) : ∃ r > 0, {T | F.IsTile T ∧ (T ∩ ball x r).Nonempty}.Finite

name: mem_coloursAt_iff_exists_tileOf
doc:
/-- The colours at a point of the domain are the colours of the tiles whose closure holds it (the rows' `P_cl`, read
tile by tile). -/
sig: theorem mem_coloursAt_iff_exists_tileOf {x : ℂ} (hx : x ∈ F.dom) {c : Fin k} : c ∈ F.coloursAt x ↔ ∃ T, F.TileOf c T ∧ x ∈ closure T

name: coneAt_region_eq_biUnion
doc:
/-- At a point of the domain, the cone of a colour class is the union of the cones of its tiles whose closure holds the
point: "the cone of a tile of colour `c`" and "the cone of the class of `c`" agree. -/
sig: theorem coneAt_region_eq_biUnion {x : ℂ} (hx : x ∈ F.dom) (c : Fin k) : coneAt (F.region c) x = ⋃ T ∈ {T | F.TileOf c T ∧ x ∈ closure T}, coneAt T x

name: exists_mem_coneAt_region
doc:
/-- At a point of the domain every direction lies in the cone of some colour (pigeonhole over the finitely many colours,
on interior points near the ray). -/
sig: theorem exists_mem_coneAt_region {x : ℂ} (hx : x ∈ F.dom) (β : ℝ) : ∃ c, β ∈ coneAt (F.region c) x

name: finite_nonring_inter_sphere
doc:
/-- Inside a ball meeting finitely many arcs, the points of the unit circle on the arcs that are not arcs of it are
finitely many. -/
sig: theorem finite_nonring_inter_sphere (p : ℂ) {y : ℂ} {ε : ℝ} (hfin : {a | a ∈ F.arcs ∧ (a.carrier ∩ ball y ε).Nonempty}.Finite) : (⋃ a ∈ {a | a ∈ F.arcs ∧ (a.carrier ∩ ball y ε).Nonempty ∧ ¬ a.OnRing p}, a.carrier ∩ sphere p 1).Finite

name: exists_ball_onRing
doc:
/-- A point of a ball meeting finitely many arcs that lies on no arc other than arcs of `ω(p)` has a neighbourhood meeting
only arcs of `ω(p)`. -/
sig: theorem exists_ball_onRing (p : ℂ) {y : ℂ} {ε : ℝ} (hfin : {a | a ∈ F.arcs ∧ (a.carrier ∩ ball y ε).Nonempty}.Finite) {x : ℂ} (hx : x ∈ ball y ε) (hxn : ∀ a ∈ F.arcs, ¬ a.OnRing p → x ∉ a.carrier) : ∃ r0 > 0, ball x r0 ⊆ ball y ε ∧ ∀ a ∈ F.arcs, (a.carrier ∩ ball x r0).Nonempty → a.OnRing p

name: exists_sides_nbhd
doc:
/-- **The sides of a ring point**: if a ball about `r(φ)` lies in the domain and meets only arcs of `ω(p)`, then for angles in a
neighbourhood of `φ` the colours just inside and just outside the ring are each one colour, the same for all of them. -/
sig: theorem exists_sides_nbhd (p : ℂ) {φ r0 : ℝ} (hr0 : 0 < r0) (hdom : ball (ringPt p φ) r0 ⊆ F.dom) (hring : ∀ a ∈ F.arcs, (a.carrier ∩ ball (ringPt p φ) r0).Nonempty → a.OnRing p) : ∃ κ > 0, ∃ c c' : Fin k, ∀ φ' ∈ Ioo (φ - κ) (φ + κ), F.innerColours p (ringPt p φ') = {c} ∧ F.outerColours p (ringPt p φ') = {c'}

name: sides_const
doc:
/-- **Constancy of the sides**: if the sides of the ring are locally constant along a preconnected set of angles, they are
constant on it. -/
sig: theorem sides_const (p : ℂ) {I : Set ℝ} (hI : IsPreconnected I) (hne : I.Nonempty) (hloc : ∀ φ ∈ I, ∃ κ > 0, ∃ c c' : Fin k, ∀ φ' ∈ Ioo (φ - κ) (φ + κ), F.innerColours p (ringPt p φ') = {c} ∧ F.outerColours p (ringPt p φ') = {c'}) : ∃ c c' : Fin k, ∀ φ ∈ I, F.innerColours p (ringPt p φ) = {c} ∧ F.outerColours p (ringPt p φ) = {c'}

name: germ_dichotomy
doc:
/-- **The germ dichotomy**: at a ring point `r(θ)` of the domain, the germ of `ω(p)` on either side lies in one colour
class, or on an arc of `Γ` on `ω(p)` with constant sides (the strip beside a short germ avoids every other arc, which
meets `ω(p)` in finitely many points). -/
sig: theorem germ_dichotomy {p : ℂ} {θ : ℝ} (hθ : ringPt p θ ∈ F.dom) (s : Side) : (∃ c, GermIn p θ s (F.region c)) ∨ ∃ θ₁ θ₂ c c', F.IsRingArc p θ₁ θ₂ c c' ∧ GermIn p θ s (ringArc p θ₁ θ₂)

name: Simple.coneAt_eq_angleIcc
doc:
/-- **In a simple map each tile's cone at a point of its closure is one closed angular interval** (possibly a single
direction, a cusp, or every direction): near the point the tile's boundary is a Jordan curve with exactly two branches,
each a segment or a circular arc, and the tile is the sector between them. -/
sig: theorem Simple.coneAt_eq_angleIcc (hS : F.Simple) {T : Set ℂ} (hT : F.IsTile T) {x : ℂ} (hxd : x ∈ F.dom) (hx : x ∈ closure T) : ∃ β₁ β₂, β₁ ≤ β₂ ∧ β₂ ≤ β₁ + 2 * π ∧ coneAt T x = angleIcc β₁ β₂

name: mem_S_add_int
doc: /-- The change set is invariant under every integer multiple of the period. -/
sig: theorem mem_S_add_int (n : ℤ) (θ : ℝ) : θ + n * (2 * π) ∈ C.S ↔ θ ∈ C.S

name: S_inter_Icc_finite
doc: /-- The change set meets every compact interval in a finite set. -/
sig: theorem S_inter_Icc_finite (a b : ℝ) : (C.S ∩ Icc a b).Finite

name: eventually_notMem_S
doc: /-- Off the point itself, the change set is eventually avoided. -/
sig: theorem eventually_notMem_S (x : ℝ) : ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[≠] x, y ∉ C.S

name: eventually_notMem_S_lt
doc: /-- Left of a point the change set is eventually avoided. -/
sig: theorem eventually_notMem_S_lt (x : ℝ) : ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[<] x, y ∉ C.S

name: eventually_notMem_S_gt
doc: /-- Right of a point the change set is eventually avoided. -/
sig: theorem eventually_notMem_S_gt (x : ℝ) : ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[>] x, y ∉ C.S

name: const_on_Ioo
doc: /-- A function locally constant at every point of an open interval is constant on it. -/
sig: theorem const_on_Ioo {β : Type*} {g : ℝ → β} {a b : ℝ} (h : ∀ y ∈ Ioo a b, ∀ᶠ y' in 𝓝 y, g y' = g y) : ∀ y ∈ Ioo a b, ∀ y' ∈ Ioo a b, g y = g y'

name: const_of_local
doc:
/-- Constancy from local agreement: on a preconnected `I`, a function whose values on a set `T` dense in `I` agree
near every point of `I` is constant on `T ∩ I`. -/
sig: theorem const_of_local {β : Type*} {I T : Set ℝ} (hI : IsPreconnected I) (hT : ∀ y ∈ I, ∀ ε > 0, ∃ z ∈ T, |z - y| < ε) {g : ℝ → β} (hg : ∀ y ∈ I, ∃ ε > 0, ∀ z ∈ T, |z - y| < ε → ∀ z' ∈ T, |z' - y| < ε → g z = g z') : ∀ z ∈ T ∩ I, ∀ z' ∈ T ∩ I, g z = g z'

name: exists_good_near
doc: /-- The complement of the change set is dense: every interval contains a point off it. -/
sig: theorem exists_good_near (y ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ z, |z - y| < ε ∧ C.Good z

name: Good.notMem
doc: /-- A good angle is off the change set. -/
sig: theorem Good.notMem {C : CircleColouring} {θ : ℝ} (h : C.Good θ) : θ ∉ C.S

name: Good.hex_notMem
doc: /-- The hexagon points `θ + i·60°`, `i ≤ 6`, of a good angle are off the change set. -/
sig: theorem Good.hex_notMem {C : CircleColouring} {θ : ℝ} (h : C.Good θ) {i : ℕ} (hi : i ≤ 6) : θ + i * (π / 3) ∉ C.S

name: exists_left_const
doc: /-- One-sided constants of a function locally constant off the change set. -/
sig: theorem exists_left_const {β : Type*} {g : ℝ → β} (hg : ∀ y ∉ C.S, ∀ᶠ y' in 𝓝 y, g y' = g y) (x : ℝ) : ∃ v, ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[<] x, g y = v

name: exists_right_const
doc: /-- One-sided constants of a function locally constant off the change set. -/
sig: theorem exists_right_const {β : Type*} {g : ℝ → β} (hg : ∀ y ∉ C.S, ∀ᶠ y' in 𝓝 y, g y' = g y) (x : ℝ) : ∃ v, ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[>] x, g y = v

name: Sides
doc: /-- `l` and `r` are the values of the lift just left and just right of `x` (equal to `f x` when `x ∉ S`). -/
sig: def Sides (x : ℝ) (l r : ℤ) : Prop

name: exists_sides
doc: /-- Every point has sides, which differ by at most one. -/
sig: theorem exists_sides (x : ℝ) : ∃ l r, L.Sides x l r ∧ |r - l| ≤ 1

name: Sides.unique
doc: /-- The sides are unique. -/
sig: theorem Sides.unique {x : ℝ} {l r l' r' : ℤ} (h : L.Sides x l r) (h' : L.Sides x l' r') : l = l' ∧ r = r'

name: Sides.vals
doc: /-- The colour just left of `x` is the cast of the left side of the lift, and likewise on the right. -/
sig: theorem Sides.vals {x : ℝ} {l r : ℤ} (h : L.Sides x l r) : C.LeftVal x (l : ZMod 3) ∧ C.RightVal x (r : ZMod 3)

name: LeftVal.unique
doc: /-- A value just left of `x` is unique. -/
sig: theorem LeftVal.unique {x : ℝ} {a b : ZMod 3} (h : C.LeftVal x a) (h' : C.LeftVal x b) : a = b

name: RightVal.unique
doc: /-- A value just right of `x` is unique. -/
sig: theorem RightVal.unique {x : ℝ} {a b : ZMod 3} (h : C.RightVal x a) (h' : C.RightVal x b) : a = b

name: eventually_lt_add
doc: /-- Shifting a left-neighbourhood statement. -/
sig: theorem eventually_lt_add {x a : ℝ} {p : ℝ → Prop} (h : ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[<] (x + a), p y) : ∀ᶠ θ in 𝓝[<] x, p (θ + a)

name: eventually_gt_add
doc: /-- Shifting a right-neighbourhood statement. -/
sig: theorem eventually_gt_add {x a : ℝ} {p : ℝ → Prop} (h : ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[>] (x + a), p y) : ∀ᶠ θ in 𝓝[>] x, p (θ + a)

name: Sides.periodic
doc: /-- The jump of the lift across `x` and across `x + 2π` agree (both lift the same change of colour, by at most one). -/
sig: theorem Sides.periodic {x : ℝ} {l r l' r' : ℤ} (h : L.Sides x l r) (h' : L.Sides (x + 2 * π) l' r') (hb : |r - l| ≤ 1) (hb' : |r' - l'| ≤ 1) : r' - l' = r - l

name: W_eq_aux
doc: /-- The winding is the same at every `θ` off `S` (`W_eq` with the lift implicit). -/
sig: theorem W_eq_aux {θ θ' : ℝ} (hθ : θ ∉ C.S) (hθ' : θ' ∉ C.S) : L.W θ = L.W θ'

name: D0_mod_ne
doc: /-- The hexagon difference vanishes mod 3 nowhere: `c(z) ≠ c(z + 60°)` lifts to `D₀(z) ≢ 0 (mod 3)`. -/
sig: theorem D0_mod_ne {z : ℝ} (hz : z ∉ C.S) (hz' : z + π / 3 ∉ C.S) : L.D 0 z % 3 ≠ 0

name: Lift.D_eq_D0
doc: /-- `D j θ` is `D 0` at the `j`-th hexagon point. -/
sig: theorem Lift.D_eq_D0 (L : C.Lift) (j : ℕ) (θ : ℝ) : L.D j θ = L.D 0 (θ + j * (π / 3))

name: step_cast
doc: /-- `step` of two casts, from the residue of the difference. -/
sig: theorem step_cast (a b : ℤ) (h : (b - a) % 3 ≠ 0) : step (a : ZMod 3) (b : ZMod 3) = if (b - a) % 3 = 2 then -1 else 1

name: D_mod_ne_good
doc: /-- At a good angle every hexagon step is nonzero mod 3. -/
sig: theorem D_mod_ne_good {θ : ℝ} (hθ : C.Good θ) {j : ℕ} (hj : j < 6) : L.D j θ % 3 ≠ 0

name: hex_summary
doc: /-- The summary of a good hexagon: `n₂ ≡ 0 (mod 3)`, `3h = 6 − 2n₂`, `3W = 3Σm + 6 + n₂`. -/
sig: theorem hex_summary {θ : ℝ} (hθ : C.Good θ) : ∃ n : ℕ, L.n₂ θ = n ∧ n % 3 = 0 ∧ n ≤ 6 ∧ C.hSum θ = 6 - 2 * (n : ℤ) ∧ L.W θ = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range 6, L.m j θ + 2 + n / 3

name: liftStep
doc:
/-- The integer step of the lift at `x`: the left and right colours' representatives `0, 1, 2` differ by at most two, and a
difference of `±2` is replaced by the step `∓1` that is congruent to it mod 3. -/
sig: noncomputable def liftStep (cl cr : ℝ → ZMod 3) (x : ℝ) : ℤ

name: liftB
doc: /-- The sum of the steps over the change points in `(a, b]`. -/
sig: noncomputable def liftB (C : CircleColouring) (cl cr : ℝ → ZMod 3) (a b : ℝ) : ℤ

name: liftA
doc: /-- The cumulative step function. -/
sig: noncomputable def liftA (C : CircleColouring) (cl cr : ℝ → ZMod 3) (θ : ℝ) : ℤ

name: liftB_fin
doc: /-- The change points in `(a, b]` are finitely many. -/
sig: theorem liftB_fin (C : CircleColouring) (a b : ℝ) : (C.S ∩ Ioc a b).Finite

name: liftB_add
doc: /-- The step sums add along consecutive intervals. -/
sig: theorem liftB_add (C : CircleColouring) (cl cr : ℝ → ZMod 3) {a b c : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) (hbc : b ≤ c) : liftB C cl cr a c = liftB C cl cr a b + liftB C cl cr b c

name: liftB_of_le
doc: /-- An empty interval has step sum zero. -/
sig: theorem liftB_of_le (C : CircleColouring) (cl cr : ℝ → ZMod 3) {a b : ℝ} (h : b ≤ a) : liftB C cl cr a b = 0

name: liftA_sub
doc: /-- The cumulative step function increases by the step sum. -/
sig: theorem liftA_sub (C : CircleColouring) (cl cr : ℝ → ZMod 3) {a b : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) : liftA C cl cr b - liftA C cl cr a = liftB C cl cr a b

name: liftB_empty
doc: /-- No change point in `(a, b]` gives step sum zero. -/
sig: theorem liftB_empty (C : CircleColouring) (cl cr : ℝ → ZMod 3) {a b : ℝ} (h : C.S ∩ Ioc a b = ∅) : liftB C cl cr a b = 0

name: liftB_single
doc: /-- One change point `x` in `(a, b]` gives the step sum `liftStep x`. -/
sig: theorem liftB_single (C : CircleColouring) (cl cr : ℝ → ZMod 3) {a b x : ℝ} (h : C.S ∩ Ioc a b = {x}) : liftB C cl cr a b = liftStep cl cr x

name: exists_lift
doc: /-- Every circle colouring has a lift (integrate the steps `±1` across the finitely many change points of a period). -/
sig: theorem exists_lift : Nonempty C.Lift

name: PairPos
doc: /-- The positions carrying two change points `60°` apart: `θ` with `θ + 60°j, θ + 60°(j + 1) ∈ S` for some `j < 6`. -/
sig: def PairPos (θ : ℝ) : Prop

name: ringband_i
sig: theorem ringband_i {θ : ℝ} (hθ : C.Good θ) : 3 * C.h θ = C.hSum θ ∧ C.hSum θ = 6 - 2 * (L.n₂ θ : ℤ) ∧ C.h θ ∈ ({-2, 0, 2} : Set ℤ)

name: ringband_ii
doc: /-- **FS129-SR1-RINGBAND** (ii): `W = m₀ + … + m₅ + 3 − h/2` at every good `θ` (and `3` divides `f(θ + 2π) − f(θ)`). -/
sig: theorem ringband_ii {θ : ℝ} (hθ : C.Good θ) : 3 ∣ L.f (θ + 2 * π) - L.f θ ∧ L.W θ = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range 6, L.m j θ + 3 - C.h θ / 2

name: W_eq
doc: /-- **FS129-SR1-RINGBAND**, the row's "put `W = (c̃(θ + 360°) − c̃(θ))/3`": the winding is the same at every `θ` off `S`. -/
sig: theorem W_eq {θ θ' : ℝ} (hθ : θ ∉ C.S) (hθ' : θ' ∉ C.S) : L.W θ = L.W θ'

name: D_eq_sub
doc: /-- `D j θ` as a difference of two hexagon values. -/
sig: theorem D_eq_sub (j : ℕ) (θ : ℝ) : L.D j θ = L.f (θ + ((j + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * (π / 3)) - L.f (θ + (j : ℝ) * (π / 3))

name: hex_near
doc: /-- Near `θ₀`, the hexagon values of a good angle are the sides of the lift at the hexagon points of `θ₀`. -/
sig: theorem hex_near (θ₀ : ℝ) : ∃ l r : ℕ → ℤ, (∀ i : ℕ, |r i - l i| ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ i : ℕ, θ₀ + (i : ℝ) * (π / 3) ∉ C.S → l i = r i) ∧ (r 6 - l 6 = r 0 - l 0) ∧ ∃ ε > 0, ∀ θ, |θ - θ₀| < ε → C.Good θ → ∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ 6 → L.f (θ + (i : ℝ) * (π / 3)) = if θ ≤ θ₀ then l i else r i

name: m_eq_near
doc: /-- Away from pairs, the thirds `m_j` agree across `θ₀`. -/
sig: theorem m_eq_near {θ₀ : ℝ} (h0 : ¬ C.PairPos θ₀) : ∃ ε > 0, ∀ θ θ', |θ - θ₀| < ε → |θ' - θ₀| < ε → C.Good θ → C.Good θ' → ∀ j < 6, L.m j θ = L.m j θ'

name: h_eq_of_m_eq
doc: /-- `h` is determined by the `m_j` and the winding. -/
sig: theorem h_eq_of_m_eq {θ θ' : ℝ} (hθ : C.Good θ) (hθ' : C.Good θ') (hm : ∀ j < 6, L.m j θ = L.m j θ') : C.h θ = C.h θ'

name: m_eq_m0
sig: theorem m_eq_m0 (j : ℕ) (θ : ℝ) : L.m j θ = L.m 0 (θ + j * (π / 3))

name: T0
doc: /-- The set where `D₀` is read: `z` and `z + 60°` off the change set. -/
sig: def T0 (C : CircleColouring) : Set ℝ

name: D0_near
doc: /-- Near any `y`, `D₀` at a point of `T0` is the left difference, the right difference, or both. -/
sig: theorem D0_near (y : ℝ) {l₀ r₀ l₁ r₁ : ℤ} (h0 : L.Sides y l₀ r₀) (h1 : L.Sides (y + π / 3) l₁ r₁) : ∃ ε > 0, ∀ z ∈ T0 C, |z - y| < ε → (z < y ∧ L.D 0 z = l₁ - l₀) ∨ (y < z ∧ L.D 0 z = r₁ - r₀) ∨ (z = y ∧ L.D 0 z = l₁ - l₀ ∧ L.D 0 z = r₁ - r₀)

name: m0_const
doc: /-- `m₀` is constant on `T0` once no step jumps by two. -/
sig: theorem m0_const (hbig : ∀ x : ℝ, ∀ l₀ r₀ l₁ r₁ : ℤ, L.Sides x l₀ r₀ → L.Sides (x + π / 3) l₁ r₁ → |r₀ - l₀| ≤ 1 → |r₁ - l₁| ≤ 1 → |(r₁ - l₁) - (r₀ - l₀)| ≤ 1) : ∀ z ∈ T0 C, ∀ z' ∈ T0 C, L.m 0 z = L.m 0 z'

name: exists_M
doc: /-- All `m_j` are one integer once `m₀` is constant on `T0`. -/
sig: theorem exists_M (hconst : ∀ z ∈ T0 C, ∀ z' ∈ T0 C, L.m 0 z = L.m 0 z') : ∃ M : ℤ, ∀ θ, C.Good θ → ∀ j < 6, L.m j θ = M

name: D0_eq
doc: /-- `D₀` as a plain difference. -/
sig: theorem D0_eq (z : ℝ) : L.D 0 z = L.f (z + π / 3) - L.f z

name: exists_T0_left
doc: /-- Just left of `x` there are points of `T0` where `D₀` is the left difference. -/
sig: theorem exists_T0_left {x : ℝ} {l₀ r₀ l₁ r₁ : ℤ} (h0 : L.Sides x l₀ r₀) (h1 : L.Sides (x + π / 3) l₁ r₁) : ∃ z ∈ T0 C, L.D 0 z = l₁ - l₀

name: exists_T0_right
doc: /-- Just right of `x` there are points of `T0` where `D₀` is the right difference. -/
sig: theorem exists_T0_right {x : ℝ} {l₀ r₀ l₁ r₁ : ℤ} (h0 : L.Sides x l₀ r₀) (h1 : L.Sides (x + π / 3) l₁ r₁) : ∃ z ∈ T0 C, L.D 0 z = r₁ - r₀

name: hbig_of_noPair
doc: /-- No two change points `60°` apart: no step jumps by two. -/
sig: theorem hbig_of_noPair (hno : ∀ x ∈ C.S, x + π / 3 ∉ C.S) : ∀ x : ℝ, ∀ l₀ r₀ l₁ r₁ : ℤ, L.Sides x l₀ r₀ → L.Sides (x + π / 3) l₁ r₁ → |r₀ - l₀| ≤ 1 → |r₁ - l₁| ≤ 1 → |(r₁ - l₁) - (r₀ - l₀)| ≤ 1

name: hbig_of_noSwap
doc: /-- No swap point: no step jumps by two. -/
sig: theorem hbig_of_noSwap (hns : ∀ x, ¬ C.IsSwap x) : ∀ x : ℝ, ∀ l₀ r₀ l₁ r₁ : ℤ, L.Sides x l₀ r₀ → L.Sides (x + π / 3) l₁ r₁ → |r₀ - l₀| ≤ 1 → |r₁ - l₁| ≤ 1 → |(r₁ - l₁) - (r₀ - l₀)| ≤ 1

name: J_eq_of_rho
doc: /-- If every `D₀` on `T0` has one residue `ρ` mod 3, the jumps at `x` and `x + 60°` agree. -/
sig: theorem J_eq_of_rho {ρ : ℤ} (hρ : ∀ z ∈ T0 C, L.D 0 z % 3 = ρ) : ∀ x : ℝ, ∀ l₀ r₀ l₁ r₁ : ℤ, L.Sides x l₀ r₀ → L.Sides (x + π / 3) l₁ r₁ → |r₀ - l₀| ≤ 1 → |r₁ - l₁| ≤ 1 → r₁ - l₁ = r₀ - l₀

name: rho_const
doc: /-- All `D₀` on `T0` have the residue forced by a nonzero common `h`. -/
sig: theorem rho_const {H : ℤ} (hh : ∀ θ, C.Good θ → C.h θ = H) (hH : H ≠ 0) : ∀ z ∈ T0 C, L.D 0 z % 3 = (if H = 2 then 1 else 2)

name: jump_ne_of_mem
doc: /-- A genuine change point has a nonzero jump. -/
sig: theorem jump_ne_of_mem (hgen : ∀ x ∈ C.S, ¬ ∃ v, C.LeftVal x v ∧ C.RightVal x v) {x : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ C.S) {l r : ℤ} (h : L.Sides x l r) : r - l ≠ 0

name: mem_of_jump_ne
doc: /-- A nonzero jump sits at a point of the change set. -/
sig: theorem mem_of_jump_ne {x : ℝ} {l r : ℤ} (h : L.Sides x l r) (hne : r - l ≠ 0) : x ∈ C.S

name: inv_of_J_eq
doc: /-- Equal jumps at `x` and `x + 60°` and genuine change points: `S` is `60°`-invariant. -/
sig: theorem inv_of_J_eq (hgen : ∀ x ∈ C.S, ¬ ∃ v, C.LeftVal x v ∧ C.RightVal x v) (hJ : ∀ x : ℝ, ∀ l₀ r₀ l₁ r₁ : ℤ, L.Sides x l₀ r₀ → L.Sides (x + π / 3) l₁ r₁ → |r₀ - l₀| ≤ 1 → |r₁ - l₁| ≤ 1 → r₁ - l₁ = r₀ - l₀) : ∀ x, x ∈ C.S ↔ x + π / 3 ∈ C.S

name: hSum_shift
doc: /-- The hexagon sum is unchanged by rotating the hexagon by `60°` (periodicity of `c`). -/
sig: theorem hSum_shift (θ : ℝ) : C.hSum (θ + π / 3) = C.hSum θ

name: ringband_iii'
doc: /-- (iii) of the row. -/
sig: theorem ringband_iii' {θ₀ : ℝ} (h0 : ¬ C.PairPos θ₀) : ∃ ε > 0, ∀ θ θ', |θ - θ₀| < ε → |θ' - θ₀| < ε → C.Good θ → C.Good θ' → C.h θ = C.h θ'

name: ringband_iii
doc: /-- **FS129-SR1-RINGBAND** (iii): `h` changes across `θ₀` only if `S` holds two points `θ₀ + 60°j` and `θ₀ + 60°(j + 1)`. -/
sig: theorem ringband_iii {θ₀ : ℝ} (h0 : ¬ C.PairPos θ₀) : ∃ ε > 0, ∀ θ θ', |θ - θ₀| < ε → |θ' - θ₀| < ε → C.Good θ → C.Good θ' → C.h θ = C.h θ'

name: ringband_iv
doc:
/-- **FS129-SR1-RINGBAND** (iv): with no swap point, all `m_j(θ)` equal one integer `M`, `W` is `6M + 2`, `6M + 3` or `6M + 4`,
and `W = 6M + 3` unless `S` is invariant under the rotation by `60°`. -/
sig: theorem ringband_iv (hns : ∀ x, ¬ C.IsSwap x) : ∃ M : ℤ, (∀ θ, C.Good θ → ∀ j < 6, L.m j θ = M) ∧ ∀ θ, C.Good θ → (L.W θ = 6 * M + 2 ∨ L.W θ = 6 * M + 3 ∨ L.W θ = 6 * M + 4) ∧ ((∀ x ∈ C.S, ¬ ∃ v, C.LeftVal x v ∧ C.RightVal x v) → (¬ ∀ x, x ∈ C.S ↔ x + π / 3 ∈ C.S) → L.W θ = 6 * M + 3)

name: ringband_v
doc:
/-- **FS129-SR1-RINGBAND** (v): with no two points of `S` `60°` apart, `h = 0` at every good `θ` and `W = 6M + 3` (`M` the
common value of the `m_j`). -/
sig: theorem ringband_v (hno : ∀ x ∈ C.S, x + π / 3 ∉ C.S) : ∃ M : ℤ, (∀ θ, C.Good θ → ∀ j < 6, L.m j θ = M) ∧ ∀ θ, C.Good θ → C.h θ = 0 ∧ L.W θ = 6 * M + 3

name: ringband_vi_periodic
doc: /-- **FS129-SR1-RINGBAND** (vi), from FS129-OA1-RINGWIND (caution C137), first clause: `h` has period `60°`. -/
sig: theorem ringband_vi_periodic {θ : ℝ} (_hθ : C.Good θ) : C.h (θ + π / 3) = C.h θ

name: ringband_vi_noJump
doc:
/-- **FS129-SR1-RINGBAND** (vi), second clause: a hexagon position that is the only one in its period with two change points
`60°` apart carries no jump of `h` (the jumps over one period sum to zero). -/
sig: theorem ringband_vi_noJump {θ₀ : ℝ} (honly : ∀ x, C.PairPos x → ∃ m : ℤ, x = θ₀ + m * (π / 3)) : ∃ ε > 0, ∀ θ θ', |θ - θ₀| < ε → |θ' - θ₀| < ε → C.Good θ → C.Good θ' → C.h θ = C.h θ'

name: exists_swap_of_abs_W_le_one

sig: theorem exists_swap_of_abs_W_le_one {θ : ℝ} (hθ : θ ∉ C.S) (hW : |L.W θ| ≤ 1) : ∃ x, C.IsSwap x

name: W_mod_six
doc: /-- **FS110-Y3-GP**, on the circle: with no two change points `60°` apart, `W ≡ 3 (mod 6)`. -/
sig: theorem W_mod_six (hno : ∀ x ∈ C.S, x + π / 3 ∉ C.S) {θ : ℝ} (hθ : θ ∉ C.S) : L.W θ % 6 = 3

name: e_injOn_Ico
doc: /-- `e` is injective on `[0, 2π)`. -/
sig: theorem e_injOn_Ico : InjOn e (Ico 0 (2 * π))

name: ring_finite_S
doc:
/-- The change set of the ring: `S = {θ | r(θ) ∈ Γ}`, finite per period on a covered ring carrying no arc of `Γ`
(`finite_ringΓ_off_ringArc`). -/
sig: theorem ring_finite_S {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (hno : ∀ x, ¬ F.OnRingArc p x) : ({θ | ringPt p θ ∈ F.Γ} ∩ Ico 0 (2 * π)).Finite

name: ring_locallyConstant
doc: /-- The ring colouring is locally constant off `S`: a ring point off `Γ` on a covered ring is an interior point. -/
sig: theorem ring_locallyConstant {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (g : Fin k → ZMod 3) : ∀ θ ∉ {θ | ringPt p θ ∈ F.Γ}, ∀ᶠ θ' in 𝓝 θ, g (F.col (ringPt p θ')) = g (F.col (ringPt p θ))

name: ring_proper
doc:
/-- The ring colouring is proper at `60°`: two ring points off `Γ` `60°` apart are at distance `1`, so have different colours
(validity), both absent at `p` (FS116-V4-TWIST), which `g` keeps apart. -/
sig: theorem ring_proper (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) {g : Fin k → ZMod 3} (hg : Set.InjOn g (F.coloursAt p)ᶜ) : ∀ θ, θ ∉ {θ | ringPt p θ ∈ F.Γ} → θ + π / 3 ∉ {θ | ringPt p θ ∈ F.Γ} → g (F.col (ringPt p θ)) ≠ g (F.col (ringPt p (θ + π / 3)))

name: ringCircleColouring
doc:
/-- **The map bridge** (FS110-N2-RING's setting): the ring of a point `p` of a valid map covering `B̄(p, 1)`, whose ring carries
no arc of `Γ`, coloured through `g : Fin k → ZMod 3` injective on the colours absent at `p`, is a circle colouring with change
set `{θ | r(θ) ∈ Γ}`. (At a three-colour vertex of a six-coloured map, `g` is any bijection of the three absent colours onto
`ℤ/3`.) -/
sig: noncomputable def ringCircleColouring (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (hno : ∀ x, ¬ F.OnRingArc p x) (g : Fin k → ZMod 3) (hg : Set.InjOn g (F.coloursAt p)ᶜ) : CircleColouring

name: exists_swap_of_ring
doc:
/-- **FS110-N2-RING**, on the map: at a point whose ring carries no arc of `Γ`, the ring colouring's winding satisfies
`|W| ≤ 1` only if the ring has a swap point. -/
sig: theorem exists_swap_of_ring (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (hno : ∀ x, ¬ F.OnRingArc p x) (g : Fin k → ZMod 3) (hg : Set.InjOn g (F.coloursAt p)ᶜ) (L : (ringCircleColouring hF hp hno g hg).Lift) {θ : ℝ} (hθ : ringPt p θ ∉ F.Γ) (hW : |L.W θ| ≤ 1) : ∃ x, (ringCircleColouring hF hp hno g hg).IsSwap x

name: Valid.false_of_crossing
doc:
/-- **The crossing lemma** (engine 1 at a closure point): in a valid map, a point `a` of the closure of the class of `c` and
a preconnected `S` inside that closure cannot hold both a point nearer than `1` to `a` and a point farther than `1`. -/
sig: theorem Valid.false_of_crossing (hF : F.Valid) {c : Fin k} {a : ℂ} (ha : a ∈ closure (F.region c)) {S : Set ℂ} (hS : IsPreconnected S) (hSc : S ⊆ closure (F.region c)) {u v : ℂ} (hu : u ∈ S) (hv : v ∈ S) (hau : dist a u < 1) (hav : 1 < dist a v) : False

name: isPreconnected_germ

name: dist_ringPt_shift_cmp
doc: /-- Two ring points `π/3 + d` apart (`|d| ≤ 1`): nearer than `1` for `d < 0`, farther for `d > 0`. -/
sig: theorem dist_ringPt_shift_cmp (p : ℂ) (α d : ℝ) (hd : |d| ≤ 1) : (d < 0 → dist (ringPt p α) (ringPt p (α + π / 3 + d)) < 1) ∧ (0 < d → 1 < dist (ringPt p α) (ringPt p (α + π / 3 + d)))

name: norm_add_sq_eq
doc: /-- The expansion of the square of a sum in coordinates. -/
sig: theorem norm_add_sq_eq (d h : ℂ) : ‖d + h‖ ^ 2 = ‖d‖ ^ 2 + 2 * (d * (starRingEnd ℂ) h).re + ‖h‖ ^ 2

name: cone_expand
doc:
/-- The first-order step of a cone argument: a point `y + h` with unit direction `u` within `ε` of `e β`, `‖d‖ = 1`:
`‖d + h‖² − 1 = ‖h‖ (2 Re(d ū) + ‖h‖)` and `|Re(d ū) − Re(d conj(e β))| ≤ ε`. -/
sig: theorem cone_expand {d h : ℂ} (hd : ‖d‖ = 1) (hh : h ≠ 0) {β ε : ℝ} (hu : ‖h / (‖h‖ : ℂ) - e β‖ < ε) : ‖d + h‖ ^ 2 - 1 = ‖h‖ * (2 * (d * (starRingEnd ℂ) (h / (‖h‖ : ℂ))).re + ‖h‖) ∧ |(d * (starRingEnd ℂ) (h / (‖h‖ : ℂ))).re - (d * (starRingEnd ℂ) (e β)).re| ≤ ε

name: dist_ringPt_germ_le
doc: /-- The distance between two ring points on one side of `r(φ₀)` and `r(φ₀)` itself is at most the angle. -/
sig: theorem dist_ringPt_germ_le (p : ℂ) (φ₀ : ℝ) (s : Side) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) : dist (ringPt p φ₀) (ringPt p (φ₀ + s.sign * t)) ≤ t

name: Valid.cone_re_nonneg_of_germ
doc:
/-- **The germ half-plane lemma, far case** (child of GERM-R): if the germ of `ω(p)` on side `s` of `w₀ = r(φ₀)` lies in
the closure of the class of `c`, `y` is at distance `1` from `w₀` and farther than `1` from the germ's points, then the
class approaches `y` only along directions `β` with `Re((y − w₀) conj e β) ≥ 0`. -/
sig: theorem Valid.cone_re_nonneg_of_germ (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} {φ₀ : ℝ} {s : Side} {c : Fin k} (h : GermIn p φ₀ s (closure (F.region c))) {y : ℂ} (hy : ‖y - ringPt p φ₀‖ = 1) (hfar : ∃ δ₀ > 0, ∀ t ∈ Ioo 0 δ₀, 1 < dist y (ringPt p (φ₀ + s.sign * t))) : ∀ β ∈ coneAt (F.region c) y, 0 ≤ ((y - ringPt p φ₀) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (e β)).re

name: Valid.cone_re_nonpos_of_germ
doc:
/-- **The germ half-plane lemma, near case** (child of GERM-R): as above with the germ's points nearer than `1` to `y`;
then `Re((y − w₀) conj e β) ≤ 0` along every direction `β` of the cone. -/
sig: theorem Valid.cone_re_nonpos_of_germ (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} {φ₀ : ℝ} {s : Side} {c : Fin k} (h : GermIn p φ₀ s (closure (F.region c))) {y : ℂ} (hy : ‖y - ringPt p φ₀‖ = 1) (hnear : ∃ δ₀ > 0, ∀ t ∈ Ioo 0 δ₀, dist y (ringPt p (φ₀ + s.sign * t)) < 1) : ∀ β ∈ coneAt (F.region c) y, ((y - ringPt p φ₀) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (e β)).re ≤ 0

name: germR_vMinus
doc:
/-- **FS116-N1-GERM-R**, `v⁻`: if the germ just clockwise of `r(ψ − 60°)` lies in the closure of the class of `c`, the class

name: germR_uPlus

name: germS_absent
doc:
/-- **FS116-N1-GERM-S**, the count: at a change point `y = r(ψ)` of the ring of a vertex `p` of at least four colours with at
most two colours absent, exactly two are absent — `X` (the ring's colour just counter-clockwise of `y`) and `X'` (`X̄`, just
clockwise). At `k = 6`: "`p` has four colours and no more, `X` and `X̄` are the colours absent at `p`". -/
sig: theorem germS_absent (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} (_hp : F.Covers p 1) (_h4 : 4 ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard) (hk : k ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard + 2) {ψ : ℝ} {X X' : Fin k} (hy : F.IsChangePoint p ψ X X') : (F.coloursAt p).ncard + 2 = k ∧ (F.coloursAt p)ᶜ = {X, X'}

doc:

doc: /-- `cos 60° = 1/2` and `sin 60° = √3/2`, the ring point `60°` on in the frame of `r(φ)`. -/

name: Valid.not_mem_closure_of_side
doc:
/-- **The crossing at a side of a ring arc** (the geometry of "a ring arc of `Γ` excludes its side colours `60°` away"): if a
ball about `r(φ)` meets the open set `O` only inside the closure of the class of `d`, where `O` holds every point whose
distance from `p` is above `1` (`s = 1`) or below `1` (`s = −1`), then `r(φ ± 60°)` is not in the closure of the class of `d`. -/
sig: theorem Valid.not_mem_closure_of_side (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} {φ : ℝ} {d : Fin k} {O : Set ℂ} {s σ ε : ℝ} (hs : s = 1 ∨ s = -1) (hσ : σ = 1 ∨ σ = -1) (hε : 0 < ε) (hO : ∀ z, 0 < s * (‖z - p‖ - 1) → z ∈ O) (hball : ball (ringPt p φ) ε ∩ O ⊆ closure (F.region d)) : p + e (φ + σ * (π / 3)) ∉ closure (F.region d)

name: dist_ringPt_third

name: IsRingArc.not_mem_closure_third
doc:
/-- **A ring arc of `Γ` excludes its side colours `60°` away**: at an interior point `r(φ)` of an arc of `Γ` on `ω(p)` with
constant sides `c`, `c'`, neither `r(φ + 60°)` nor `r(φ − 60°)` lies in the closure of the class of `c` or of `c'`. -/
sig: theorem IsRingArc.not_mem_closure_third (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} {θ₁ θ₂ : ℝ} {c c' : Fin k} (hA : F.IsRingArc p θ₁ θ₂ c c') {φ : ℝ} (hφ : φ ∈ Ioo θ₁ θ₂) {σ : ℝ} (hσ : σ = 1 ∨ σ = -1) : ringPt p (φ + σ * (π / 3)) ∉ closure (F.region c) ∧ ringPt p (φ + σ * (π / 3)) ∉ closure (F.region c')

name: carries_absent
doc:
/-- **A regular ring point not on a (Q) arc carries the one absent colour, and its `60°` neighbours do not.** With every
absent colour equal to `X` (so at most one absent colour), a regular ring point `r(θ)` of a vertex of at least four colours,
on no (Q) arc, lies in the closure of the class of `X`, while `r(θ ± 60°)` do not. -/
sig: theorem carries_absent (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (h4 : 4 ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard) {X : Fin k} (hab : ∀ d, d ∉ F.coloursAt p → d = X) {θ : ℝ} (hQ : ¬ F.OnQArc p (ringPt p θ)) (hreg : F.RegularAt p θ) : ringPt p θ ∈ closure (F.region X) ∧ ∀ σ : ℝ, (σ = 1 ∨ σ = -1) → ringPt p (θ + σ * (π / 3)) ∉ closure (F.region X)
