name: exists_regular_germ
doc:
/-- **Every side germ of the ring is regular**: near any ring point, on each side, all the angles are regular (off `Γ`, or
interior to an arc with constant sides: the germ dichotomy, less the at most two points of the germ at an end of the arc). -/
sig: theorem exists_regular_germ {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (θ : ℝ) (s : Side) : ∃ δ > 0, ∀ t ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) δ, F.RegularAt p (θ + s.sign * t)

name: finite_not_regular
doc:
/-- **The irregular angles of a bounded range are finitely many**: they form a closed set, each of whose points has no other
irregular angle on either side nearby. -/
sig: theorem finite_not_regular {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (N : ℝ) : {θ | θ ∈ Icc 0 N ∧ ¬ F.RegularAt p θ}.Finite

name: absent_subsingleton
doc: /-- At most one colour is absent at `p` when `k ≤ (colours at p) + 1`: any two absent colours agree. -/
sig: theorem absent_subsingleton {p : ℂ} (hk : k ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard + 1) : ∀ a b, a ∉ F.coloursAt p → b ∉ F.coloursAt p → a = b

name: exists_regular_pair
doc: /-- Two regular ring angles `60°` apart exist. -/
sig: theorem exists_regular_pair {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) : ∃ θ, F.RegularAt p θ ∧ F.RegularAt p (θ + π / 3)

name: qfree4
doc:
/-- **FS116-N1-QFREE4** (at every `k`: the argument reads that at least two colours are absent): at a vertex of at least four
colours whose ring carries no (Q) arc, at least two colours are absent. At `k = 6`: "`p` has four colours and no more". -/
sig: theorem qfree4 (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (h4 : 4 ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard) (hq : ∀ θ₁ θ₂, ¬ F.IsQArc p θ₁ θ₂) : (F.coloursAt p).ncard + 2 ≤ k

name: fiveRing_no_changePoint
doc:
/-- **FS116-N2-FIVERING**, first clause (and FS116-RING-TRANSFER-C's "a ring of five colours has no change point"): the ring
of a vertex of at least four colours with exactly one colour absent has no change point. -/
sig: theorem fiveRing_no_changePoint (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} (_hp : F.Covers p 1) (_h4 : 4 ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard) (hk : (F.coloursAt p).ncard + 1 = k) (ψ : ℝ) (X X' : Fin k) : ¬ F.IsChangePoint p ψ X X'

name: fiveRing_finite_off_Q
doc: /-- **FS116-N2-FIVERING**: for every `θ` outside a finite set, `r(θ)` or `r(θ + 60°)` lies on a (Q) arc. -/
sig: theorem fiveRing_finite_off_Q (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (h4 : 4 ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard) (hk : (F.coloursAt p).ncard + 1 = k) : {θ | θ ∈ Ico 0 (2 * π) ∧ ¬ F.OnQArc p (ringPt p θ) ∧ ¬ F.OnQArc p (ringPt p (θ + π / 3))}.Finite

name: qOpen
doc: /-- The angles interior to the open interval of some (Q) arc of the ring of `p`. -/
sig: def qOpen (F : ArcMap k) (p : ℂ) : Set ℝ

name: qOpen_subset
doc: /-- Angles interior to a (Q) arc are on a closed (Q) arc. -/
sig: theorem qOpen_subset (F : ArcMap k) (p : ℂ) : qOpen F p ⊆ {θ | F.OnQArc p (ringPt p θ)}

name: isOpen_qOpen
doc: /-- `qOpen` is open. -/
sig: theorem isOpen_qOpen (F : ArcMap k) (p : ℂ) : IsOpen (qOpen F p)

name: qOpen_periodic
doc: /-- `qOpen` is `2π`-periodic. -/
sig: theorem qOpen_periodic (F : ArcMap k) (p : ℂ) (θ : ℝ) : θ + 2 * π ∈ qOpen F p ↔ θ ∈ qOpen F p

name: qOpen_of_regular
doc:
/-- **A regular angle on a closed (Q) arc is interior to a (Q) arc**: the arc of constant sides through a regular angle has
the colours of any (Q) arc that reaches the angle, so is (Q) itself. -/
sig: theorem qOpen_of_regular {p : ℂ} {θ : ℝ} (hreg : F.RegularAt p θ) (hQ : F.OnQArc p (ringPt p θ)) : θ ∈ qOpen F p

name: arcLength_apply
doc: /-- Arc-length of a set equals the Lebesgue measure of its part in `[0, 2π)`. -/
sig: theorem arcLength_apply (A : Set ℝ) : arcLength A = volume (A ∩ Ico 0 (2 * π))

name: arcLength_preimage_add_periodic
doc: /-- **Arc-length is invariant under a shift, on measurable `2π`-periodic sets.** -/
sig: theorem arcLength_preimage_add_periodic {O : Set ℝ} (hO : MeasurableSet O) (hper : ∀ θ, θ + 2 * π ∈ O ↔ θ ∈ O) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) (hc2 : c ≤ 2 * π) : arcLength ((fun θ => θ + c) ⁻¹' O) = arcLength O

name: fiveRing_length
doc:
/-- **FS116-N2-FIVERING** (and FS112-SIX's five-colour clause): the (Q) arcs of the ring have total length at least `180°`
(arc-length of the set of angles in `[0, 2π)` whose ring point lies on a closed (Q) arc). -/
sig: theorem fiveRing_length (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (h4 : 4 ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard) (hk : (F.coloursAt p).ncard + 1 = k) : ENNReal.ofReal π ≤ arcLength {θ | F.OnQArc p (ringPt p θ)}

name: fiveRing_no_hub
doc: /-- **FS116-N2-FIVERING**, last clause (and FS116-RING-TRANSFER-C's "places no vertex through RING-GERM"): `p` has no hub. -/
sig: theorem fiveRing_no_hub (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (h4 : 4 ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard) (hk : (F.coloursAt p).ncard + 1 = k) (ψ : ℝ) : ¬ F.IsHub p ψ

name: sixQ_sphere_subset_Γ
doc:
/-- **FS129-SR1-SIXQ** (carrying FS112-SIX's "its whole unit circle lies in `Γ`"): at a point carrying all `k` colours, on a
covered ring, `ω(p)` lies in `Γ`. -/
sig: theorem sixQ_sphere_subset_Γ (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (hall : F.coloursAt p = univ) : sphere p 1 ⊆ F.Γ

name: sixQ_sides
doc: /-- **FS129-SR1-SIXQ**: both side colours of every arc of `Γ` on `ω(p)` are carried at `p`. -/
sig: theorem sixQ_sides {p : ℂ} (hall : F.coloursAt p = univ) {θ₁ θ₂ : ℝ} {c c' : Fin k} (_hA : F.IsRingArc p θ₁ θ₂ c c') : c ∈ F.coloursAt p ∧ c' ∈ F.coloursAt p

name: sixQ_isQArc
doc:
/-- **FS129-SR1-SIXQ**, the (Q) clause (at every `k ≥ 4`; the row is `k = 6`, "every arc of kind both" of FS112-SIX): when
`p` carries all colours, every arc of `Γ` on `ω(p)` is a (Q) arc. -/
sig: theorem sixQ_isQArc (hk : 4 ≤ k) {p : ℂ} (hall : F.coloursAt p = univ) {θ₁ θ₂ : ℝ} {c c' : Fin k} (h : F.IsRingArc p θ₁ θ₂ c c') : F.IsQArc p θ₁ θ₂

name: sixQ_inhabited
doc:
/-- SIXQ's hypotheses are inhabited by FS116-Y2-SIXFRAG: a valid six-coloured fragment covering `B̄(0, 1)` with all six
colours at `0`, and an arc of `Γ` on `ω(0)`. -/
sig: theorem sixQ_inhabited : sixFrag.Valid ∧ sixFrag.Covers 0 1 ∧ sixFrag.coloursAt 0 = univ ∧ sixFrag.IsRingArc 0 0 (π / 6) 0 2

name: exists_near_of_mem_closure_isOpen
doc: /-- An open set whose closure holds `x` has points of it other than `x` arbitrarily near `x`. -/
sig: theorem exists_near_of_mem_closure_isOpen {T : Set ℂ} (hTo : IsOpen T) {x : ℂ} (hx : x ∈ closure T) : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ z ∈ T, z ≠ x ∧ dist z x < ε

name: not_mem_closure_of_four_germs
doc:
/-- **The four germs at `r(ψ ± 60°)` in the closure of one class keep the class away from `r(ψ)`**: GERM-R's four open
direction sets cover every direction. -/
sig: theorem not_mem_closure_of_four_germs (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} {ψ : ℝ} {c : Fin k} (h1 : GermIn p (ψ - π / 3) .cw (closure (F.region c))) (h2 : GermIn p (ψ - π / 3) .ccw (closure (F.region c))) (h3 : GermIn p (ψ + π / 3) .cw (closure (F.region c))) (h4 : GermIn p (ψ + π / 3) .ccw (closure (F.region c))) : ringPt p ψ ∉ closure (F.region c)

name: exists_germ_interior
doc:
/-- **A germ on a ring arc is, off at most two angles, interior to the arc**: near a ring point, on one side, every angle of
the germ is congruent to an interior angle of the arc. -/
sig: theorem exists_germ_interior {p : ℂ} {θ₁ θ₂ : ℝ} {θ : ℝ} {s : Side} (hg : GermIn p θ s (ringArc p θ₁ θ₂)) : ∃ δ > 0, ∀ t ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) δ, ∃ ψ ∈ Ioo θ₁ θ₂, e ψ = e (θ + s.sign * t)

name: IsRingArc.ringArc_subset_closure
doc: /-- The whole closed arc of a ring arc lies in the closure of each side colour's class. -/
sig: theorem IsRingArc.ringArc_subset_closure {p : ℂ} {θ₁ θ₂ : ℝ} {c c' : Fin k} (hA : F.IsRingArc p θ₁ θ₂ c c') : ringArc p θ₁ θ₂ ⊆ closure (F.region c) ∧ ringArc p θ₁ θ₂ ⊆ closure (F.region c')

name: IsRingArc.eq_of_mem_closure
doc: /-- **An interior point of a ring arc lies in the closure of a class only if the class is a side colour**. -/
sig: theorem IsRingArc.eq_of_mem_closure {p : ℂ} {θ₁ θ₂ : ℝ} {c c' : Fin k} (hA : F.IsRingArc p θ₁ θ₂ c c') {φ : ℝ} (hφ : φ ∈ Ioo θ₁ θ₂) {X : Fin k} (hX : ringPt p φ ∈ closure (F.region X)) : X = c ∨ X = c'

name: germ_absent_class
doc:
/-- **A germ off a (Q) arc, with `X` absent and not in the germ's closure: it lies with the other absent colour `X'`.** With
exactly the colours `X`, `X'` absent at `p` and `X ≠ X'`, a germ of the ring that lies on no (Q) arc and not in the closure of
the class of `X` lies in the closure of the class of `X'` and misses the closure of the class of `X`. -/
sig: theorem germ_absent_class (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (h4 : 4 ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard) {X X' : Fin k} (hXX' : X ≠ X') (hcompl : (F.coloursAt p)ᶜ = {X, X'}) {θ : ℝ} (s : Side) (hQ : ¬ F.GermOnQ p θ s) (hnoX : ¬ GermIn p θ s (closure (F.region X))) : GermIn p θ s (closure (F.region X')) ∧ GermIn p θ s (closure (F.region X))ᶜ

name: mem_ringArc_of_germIn
doc: /-- A germ of the ring inside a closed sub-arc of the ring: its base point lies in the sub-arc. -/
sig: theorem mem_ringArc_of_germIn {p : ℂ} {ψ θ₁ θ₂ : ℝ} {s : Side} (hg : GermIn p ψ s (ringArc p θ₁ θ₂)) : ringPt p ψ ∈ ringArc p θ₁ θ₂

name: touchW
doc:
/-- **FS129-SR2-TOUCHW** (carrying FS116-N1-TOUCH, its idle hypothesis "w in the closure of a tile of one of `p`'s colours"
dropped): at a vertex of at least four colours with exactly two colours absent, let `w = r(ψ)` be no change point, on no arc
of `Γ` on `ω(p)`, with none of the four germs at `ψ ± 60°` on a (Q) arc. Then the ring just clockwise and just
counter-clockwise of `w` lies in one col
sig: theorem touchW (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (h4 : 4 ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard) (hk : (F.coloursAt p).ncard + 2 = k) {ψ : ℝ} (hnc : ∀ X X', ¬ F.IsChangePoint p ψ X X') (hna : ¬ F.OnRingArc p (ringPt p ψ)) (hq : ∀ s, ¬ F.GermOnQ p (ψ + π / 3) s ∧ ¬ F.GermOnQ p (ψ - π / 3) s) : ∃ X X', X ≠ X' ∧ (F.coloursAt p)ᶜ = {X, X'} ∧ GermIn p ψ .cw (F.region X) ∧ GermIn p ψ .ccw (F.region X) ∧ (∀ θ ∈ ({ψ + π / 3, ψ - π / 3} : Set ℝ), ∀ s, GermIn p θ s (closure (F.region X')) ∧ GermIn p θ s (closure (F.region X))ᶜ) ∧ X' ∉ F.coloursAt (ringPt p ψ)

name: echo_unique
doc:
/-- **FS116-N1-ECHO**, the engine: if the ring just clockwise and just counter-clockwise of `w = r(ψ)` lies in the class of a
colour `X` absent at `p`, the only point of the closure of the class of `X` at distance `1` from `w` is `2w − p`. -/
sig: theorem echo_unique (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} {ψ : ℝ} {X : Fin k} (hcw : GermIn p ψ .cw (F.region X)) (hccw : GermIn p ψ .ccw (F.region X)) (hX : X ∉ F.coloursAt p) {x : ℂ} (hx : x ∈ closure (F.region X)) (h1 : dist x (ringPt p ψ) = 1) : x = 2 * ringPt p ψ - p

name: echo_of_mem_closure
doc:
/-- **FS116-N1-ECHO** at the class its argument reads: some point of the closure of the class of `X` at distance `1` from `w`
puts `2w − p` in that closure. -/
sig: theorem echo_of_mem_closure (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} {ψ : ℝ} {X : Fin k} (hcw : GermIn p ψ .cw (F.region X)) (hccw : GermIn p ψ .ccw (F.region X)) (hX : X ∉ F.coloursAt p) (hpt : ∃ x ∈ closure (F.region X), dist x (ringPt p ψ) = 1) : X ∈ F.coloursAt (2 * ringPt p ψ - p)

name: echo
doc:
/-- **FS116-N1-ECHO**, the row's form (reading (B)): if `w` is an essential boundary point at which the map is saturated and
`X` is in `w`'s essential multicolour, `2w − p` lies in the closure of the class of `X`. -/
sig: theorem echo (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} {ψ : ℝ} {X : Fin k} (hcw : GermIn p ψ .cw (F.region X)) (hccw : GermIn p ψ .ccw (F.region X)) (hX : X ∉ F.coloursAt p) (_hess : F.IsEssBoundary (ringPt p ψ)) (hsat : F.SaturatedAt (ringPt p ψ)) (hXw : X ∈ F.essColours (ringPt p ψ)) : X ∈ F.coloursAt (2 * ringPt p ψ - p)

name: norm_sub_sq_eq
doc: /-- `‖a − b‖²` in terms of `Re(a b̄)`. -/
sig: theorem norm_sub_sq_eq (a b : ℂ) : ‖a - b‖ ^ 2 = ‖a‖ ^ 2 - 2 * (a * (starRingEnd ℂ) b).re + ‖b‖ ^ 2

name: norm_sq_sub_radial
doc: /-- The distance from `z + h` to the radial point `z + t e θ`, squared. -/
sig: theorem norm_sq_sub_radial (h : ℂ) (t θ : ℝ) : ‖h - (t : ℂ) * e θ‖ ^ 2 = ‖h‖ ^ 2 - 2 * t * (h * (starRingEnd ℂ) (e θ)).re + t ^ 2

name: re_mul_conj_e_bound
doc:
/-- Re(h ē θ) in terms of a cone direction: for `h ≠ 0` with `‖h/‖h‖ − e β‖ < ε`,
`|Re(h conj eθ) − ‖h‖ cos(β − θ)| ≤ ‖h‖ ε`. -/
sig: theorem re_mul_conj_e_bound {h : ℂ} (hh : h ≠ 0) {β θ ε : ℝ} (hu : ‖h / (‖h‖ : ℂ) - e β‖ < ε) : |(h * (starRingEnd ℂ) (e θ)).re - ‖h‖ * Real.cos (β - θ)| ≤ ‖h‖ * ε

name: changePoint_germs
doc:
/-- **At a change point, the four germs at `ψ ± 60°` carry the two absent colours, by the rotation and the dichotomy**:
`v⁻` and `u⁻` carry `X`, `v⁺` and `u⁺` carry `X'` (given none lies on a (Q) arc). -/
sig: theorem changePoint_germs (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (h4 : 4 ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard) {ψ : ℝ} {X X' : Fin k} (hy : F.IsChangePoint p ψ X X') (hcompl : (F.coloursAt p)ᶜ = {X, X'}) : (¬ F.GermOnQ p (ψ - π / 3) .cw → GermIn p (ψ - π / 3) .cw (closure (F.region X))) ∧ (¬ F.GermOnQ p (ψ + π / 3) .ccw → GermIn p (ψ + π / 3) .ccw (closure (F.region X')))

name: tile_subset_closedBall_of_cone
doc:
/-- **Tiles of `p` of a colour that approaches `y = r(ψ)` from the side of `p` lie in `B̄(y, 1)`**: if the class of `c`
approaches `y` along `β` with `cos(β − ψ) < 0`, every tile of colour `c` with `p` in its closure lies in `B̄(y, 1)`. -/
sig: theorem tile_subset_closedBall_of_cone (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} {ψ β : ℝ} {c : Fin k} (hcos : Real.cos (β - ψ) < 0) (hβ : β ∈ coneAt (F.region c) (ringPt p ψ)) {A : Set ℂ} (hA : F.TileOf c A) (hpA : p ∈ closure A) : A ⊆ closedBall (ringPt p ψ) 1

name: germS_inward
doc:
/-- **FS116-N1-GERM-S** (i): if neither `v⁻` nor `u⁺` lies on a (Q) arc, every direction at `y` in the open `60°` cone about
the direction to `p` lies in the cone of a colour `c` of `p` every tile of `p` of which colour lies in `B̄(y, 1)`. -/
sig: theorem germS_inward (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (h4 : 4 ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard) (hk : k ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard + 2) {ψ : ℝ} {X X' : Fin k} (hy : F.IsChangePoint p ψ X X') (hv : ¬ F.GermOnQ p (ψ - π / 3) .cw) (hu : ¬ F.GermOnQ p (ψ + π / 3) .ccw) : ∀ β ∈ Ioo (ψ + 5 * π / 6) (ψ + 7 * π / 6), ∃ c ∈ F.coloursAt p, β ∈ coneAt (F.region c) (ringPt p ψ) ∧ ∀ A, F.TileOf c A → p ∈ closure A → A ⊆ closedBall (ringPt p ψ) 1

name: outward_of_cone
doc:
/-- **Away from `p`: the cone of a class along `β` with `cos(β − ψ) > 0` is the cone of its part outside `B̄(p, 1)`, and the
tiles of `p` of that colour miss `B(y, 1)`.** -/
sig: theorem outward_of_cone (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} {ψ β : ℝ} {c : Fin k} (hcos : 0 < Real.cos (β - ψ)) (hβ : β ∈ coneAt (F.region c) (ringPt p ψ)) : β ∈ coneAt (F.region c \ closedBall p 1) (ringPt p ψ) ∧ ∀ A, F.TileOf c A → p ∈ closure A → Disjoint A (ball (ringPt p ψ) 1)

name: changePoint_germs_out
doc: /-- The other two of the four germs at a change point: `u⁻` carries `X` and `v⁺` carries `X'`. -/
sig: theorem changePoint_germs_out (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (h4 : 4 ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard) {ψ : ℝ} {X X' : Fin k} (hy : F.IsChangePoint p ψ X X') (hcompl : (F.coloursAt p)ᶜ = {X, X'}) : (¬ F.GermOnQ p (ψ + π / 3) .cw → GermIn p (ψ + π / 3) .cw (closure (F.region X))) ∧ (¬ F.GermOnQ p (ψ - π / 3) .ccw → GermIn p (ψ - π / 3) .ccw (closure (F.region X')))

name: germS_outward
doc:
/-- **FS116-N1-GERM-S** (ii): if neither `u⁻` nor `v⁺` lies on a (Q) arc, every direction at `y` in the open `60°` cone about
the direction away from `p` lies in the cone of a tile, not a tile of `p`, of a colour `c` of `p` every tile of `p` of which
colour misses `B(y, 1)`. "A tile, not a tile of `p`" is the part of the class outside `B̄(p, 1)`, which no tile of `p` meets
(`IsTile.subset_ball`);
sig: theorem germS_outward (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (h4 : 4 ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard) (hk : k ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard + 2) {ψ : ℝ} {X X' : Fin k} (hy : F.IsChangePoint p ψ X X') (hu : ¬ F.GermOnQ p (ψ + π / 3) .cw) (hv : ¬ F.GermOnQ p (ψ - π / 3) .ccw) : ∀ β ∈ Ioo (ψ - π / 6) (ψ + π / 6), ∃ c ∈ F.coloursAt p, β ∈ coneAt (F.region c \ closedBall p 1) (ringPt p ψ) ∧ ∀ A, F.TileOf c A → p ∈ closure A → Disjoint A (ball (ringPt p ψ) 1)

name: germS_four
doc:
/-- **FS116-N1-GERM-S** (iii): if none of the four germs at `ψ ± 60°` lies on a (Q) arc, `y` is a vertex of at least four
colours. -/
sig: theorem germS_four (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (h4 : 4 ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard) (hk : k ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard + 2) {ψ : ℝ} {X X' : Fin k} (hy : F.IsChangePoint p ψ X X') (hq : ∀ s, ¬ F.GermOnQ p (ψ + π / 3) s ∧ ¬ F.GermOnQ p (ψ - π / 3) s) : 4 ≤ (F.coloursAt (ringPt p ψ)).ncard

name: ringQPrimeS
doc:
/-- **FS116-RING-Q-PRIME-S** (carrying FS116-RING-Q-PRIME; at every `k` with at most two colours absent): a change point of
the ring of a vertex of at least four colours whose points at `±60°` lie on no closed (Q) arc is a vertex of at least four
colours. -/
sig: theorem ringQPrimeS (hF : F.Valid) {p : ℂ} (hp : F.Covers p 1) (h4 : 4 ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard) (hk : k ≤ (F.coloursAt p).ncard + 2) {ψ : ℝ} {X X' : Fin k} (hy : F.IsChangePoint p ψ X X') (hu : ¬ F.OnQArc p (ringPt p (ψ + π / 3))) (hv : ¬ F.OnQArc p (ringPt p (ψ - π / 3))) : 4 ≤ (F.coloursAt (ringPt p ψ)).ncard

name: Valid.cos_nonneg_of_radial_inner
doc:
/-- **The radial lemma, inner side** (child of FS116-V5-U1): if the radial segment `z + t e θ`, `t ∈ (1 − η₀, 1)`, lies in
the closure of the class of `c`, the class approaches `z` only along directions `β` with `cos(β − θ) ≥ 0`. -/
sig: theorem Valid.cos_nonneg_of_radial_inner (hF : F.Valid) {z : ℂ} {θ : ℝ} {c : Fin k} {η₀ : ℝ} (hη₀ : 0 < η₀) (hseg : ∀ t ∈ Ioo (1 - η₀) 1, z + (t : ℂ) * e θ ∈ closure (F.region c)) : ∀ β ∈ coneAt (F.region c) z, 0 ≤ Real.cos (β - θ)

name: outer_near_arith
doc: /-- Arithmetic of the outer radial lemma, near point. -/
sig: theorem outer_near_arith {ρ κ R x : ℝ} (hρ0 : 0 < ρ) (hκ0 : 0 < κ) (hκ1 : κ ≤ 1) (hρκ : ρ ≤ κ / 4) (hR : ρ * κ * (3 / 4) ≤ R) (hx : x = κ * ρ / 2) : ρ ^ 2 - 2 * (1 + x) * R + (1 + x) ^ 2 < 1

name: outer_far_arith
doc: /-- Arithmetic of the outer radial lemma, far point. -/
sig: theorem outer_far_arith {ρ R : ℝ} (hρ0 : 0 < ρ) (hR : R ≤ ρ) : 1 < ρ ^ 2 - 2 * (1 + 2 * ρ) * R + (1 + 2 * ρ) ^ 2

name: Valid.cos_nonpos_of_radial_outer
doc:
/-- **The radial lemma, outer side** (child of FS116-V5-U1): if the radial segment `z + t e θ`, `t ∈ (1, 1 + η₀)`, lies in
the closure of the class of `c'`, the class approaches `z` only along directions `β` with `cos(β − θ) ≤ 0`. -/
sig: theorem Valid.cos_nonpos_of_radial_outer (hF : F.Valid) {z : ℂ} {θ : ℝ} {c : Fin k} {η₀ : ℝ} (hη₀ : 0 < η₀) (hseg : ∀ t ∈ Ioo 1 (1 + η₀), z + (t : ℂ) * e θ ∈ closure (F.region c)) : ∀ β ∈ coneAt (F.region c) z, Real.cos (β - θ) ≤ 0

name: mem_angleIcc_of_cos_nonneg
doc: /-- Cosine nonnegative against every angle of `(θ₁, θ₂)` puts `β` in the angular interval `[θ₂ − 90°, θ₁ + 90°]`. -/
sig: theorem mem_angleIcc_of_cos_nonneg {θ₁ θ₂ β : ℝ} (h12 : θ₁ < θ₂) (h : ∀ θ ∈ Ioo θ₁ θ₂, 0 ≤ Real.cos (β - θ)) : β ∈ angleIcc (θ₂ - π / 2) (θ₁ + π / 2)

name: IsRingArc.radial_inner
doc: /-- The radial segment just inside an arc of `Γ` on `ω(z)` lies in the closure of the inner colour's class. -/
sig: theorem IsRingArc.radial_inner {z : ℂ} {θ₁ θ₂ : ℝ} {c c' : Fin k} (hA : F.IsRingArc z θ₁ θ₂ c c') {θ : ℝ} (hθ : θ ∈ Ioo θ₁ θ₂) : ∃ η₀ : ℝ, 0 < η₀ ∧ ∀ t ∈ Ioo (1 - η₀) 1, z + (t : ℂ) * e θ ∈ closure (F.region c)

name: IsRingArc.radial_outer
doc: /-- The radial segment just outside an arc of `Γ` on `ω(z)` lies in the closure of the outer colour's class. -/
sig: theorem IsRingArc.radial_outer {z : ℂ} {θ₁ θ₂ : ℝ} {c c' : Fin k} (hA : F.IsRingArc z θ₁ θ₂ c c') {θ : ℝ} (hθ : θ ∈ Ioo θ₁ θ₂) : ∃ η₀ : ℝ, 0 < η₀ ∧ ∀ t ∈ Ioo 1 (1 + η₀), z + (t : ℂ) * e θ ∈ closure (F.region c')

name: disjoint_angleIcc_angleIoo_of_le
doc: /-- Angular intervals `[A, B]` and `(C, D)` are disjoint when `D ≤ A` and `B ≤ C + 2π`. -/
sig: theorem disjoint_angleIcc_angleIoo_of_le {A B C D : ℝ} (h1 : D ≤ A) (h2 : B ≤ C + 2 * π) : Disjoint (angleIcc A B) (angleIoo C D)

name: disjoint_angleIcc_angleIoo_of_le'
doc: /-- Angular intervals `[A, B]` and `(C, D)` are disjoint when `B ≤ C` and `D ≤ A + 2π`. -/
sig: theorem disjoint_angleIcc_angleIoo_of_le' {A B C D : ℝ} (h1 : B ≤ C) (h2 : D ≤ A + 2 * π) : Disjoint (angleIcc A B) (angleIoo C D)

name: ringArc_cone_inner
doc:
/-- **FS116-V5-U1**, inner side: if `A = r([θ₁, θ₂])` (about `z`) is an arc of `Γ` on `ω(z)` with inner colour `c`, the class
of `c` approaches `z` only within the closed cone `[θ₂ − 90°, θ₁ + 90°]` facing `A`. -/
sig: theorem ringArc_cone_inner (hF : F.Valid) {z : ℂ} {θ₁ θ₂ : ℝ} {c c' : Fin k} (hA : F.IsRingArc z θ₁ θ₂ c c') : coneAt (F.region c) z ⊆ angleIcc (θ₂ - π / 2) (θ₁ + π / 2)

name: ringArc_cone_outer
doc:
/-- **FS116-V5-U1**, outer side: the class of the outer colour `c'` approaches `z` only within the closed cone
`[θ₂ + 90°, θ₁ + 270°]` facing away from `A`. -/
sig: theorem ringArc_cone_outer (hF : F.Valid) {z : ℂ} {θ₁ θ₂ : ℝ} {c c' : Fin k} (hA : F.IsRingArc z θ₁ θ₂ c c') : coneAt (F.region c') z ⊆ angleIcc (θ₂ + π / 2) (θ₁ + 3 * π / 2)

name: ringArc_sideCone_inner
doc: /-- **FS116-V5-U1**: the open side cone `(θ₁ − 90°, θ₂ − 90°)` holds neither side colour. -/
sig: theorem ringArc_sideCone_inner (hF : F.Valid) {z : ℂ} {θ₁ θ₂ : ℝ} {c c' : Fin k} (hA : F.IsRingArc z θ₁ θ₂ c c') : Disjoint (coneAt (F.region c) z ∪ coneAt (F.region c') z) (angleIoo (θ₁ - π / 2) (θ₂ - π / 2))

name: ringArc_sideCone_outer
doc: /-- **FS116-V5-U1**: the open side cone `(θ₁ + 90°, θ₂ + 90°)` holds neither side colour. -/
sig: theorem ringArc_sideCone_outer (hF : F.Valid) {z : ℂ} {θ₁ θ₂ : ℝ} {c c' : Fin k} (hA : F.IsRingArc z θ₁ θ₂ c c') : Disjoint (coneAt (F.region c) z ∪ coneAt (F.region c') z) (angleIoo (θ₁ + π / 2) (θ₂ + π / 2))

name: ringArc_sideCone_other
doc:
/-- **FS116-V5-U1**, "the side cones hold two further colours": at a point `z` of the domain, every direction of either open
side cone lies in the cone of a colour other than `c` and `c'`. (`z ∈ F.dom` is a hypothesis the row leaves implicit: off
the domain a side cone may hold no colour at all — plan § 3.3.) -/
sig: theorem ringArc_sideCone_other (hF : F.Valid) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ F.dom) {θ₁ θ₂ : ℝ} {c c' : Fin k} (hA : F.IsRingArc z θ₁ θ₂ c c') {β : ℝ} (hβ : β ∈ angleIoo (θ₁ - π / 2) (θ₂ - π / 2) ∪ angleIoo (θ₁ + π / 2) (θ₂ + π / 2)) : ∃ d, d ≠ c ∧ d ≠ c' ∧ β ∈ coneAt (F.region d) z

name: four_of_bothKind
doc:
/-- **FS116-V5-U1**, the four-colour clause at the class it reads: if `z` (in the domain) carries both side colours of an arc
of `Γ` on `ω(z)` (the arc is both-kind), each colour has at most one tile with `z` in its closure, and each such tile's cone
at `z` is one closed angular interval of positive length (`β₁ < β₂`: no cusp at `z`; inventory item 112), then `z` carries at
least four colours. -/
sig: theorem four_of_bothKind (hF : F.Valid) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ F.dom) {θ₁ θ₂ : ℝ} {c c' : Fin k} (hA : F.IsRingArc z θ₁ θ₂ c c') (hc : c ∈ F.coloursAt z) (hc' : c' ∈ F.coloursAt z) (hone : ∀ d T T', F.TileOf d T → F.TileOf d T' → z ∈ closure T → z ∈ closure T' → T = T') (hint : ∀ T, F.IsTile T → z ∈ closure T → ∃ β₁ β₂, β₁ < β₂ ∧ β₂ ≤ β₁ + 2 * π ∧ coneAt T z = angleIcc β₁ β₂) : 4 ≤ (F.coloursAt z).ncard

name: four_of_bothKind_simple
doc:
/-- **FS116-V5-U1**, the row's four-colour clause: in a non-Siamese simple map, a point `z` of the domain carrying both side
colours of an arc of `Γ` on `ω(z)` carries at least four colours, provided no tile with `z` in its closure has a cone reduced to
one direction (`hnc`: no cusp at `z`; inventory item 112). -/
sig: theorem four_of_bothKind_simple (hF : F.Valid) (hN : F.NonSiamese) (hS : F.Simple) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ F.dom) {θ₁ θ₂ : ℝ} {c c' : Fin k} (hA : F.IsRingArc z θ₁ θ₂ c c') (hc : c ∈ F.coloursAt z) (hc' : c' ∈ F.coloursAt z) (hnc : ∀ T, F.IsTile T → z ∈ closure T → ∀ β, coneAt T z ≠ angleIcc β β) : 4 ≤ (F.coloursAt z).ncard

name: mem_angleIcc_of_cos_nonneg_single
doc: /-- Cosine nonnegative against one angle `γ` puts `β` in the angular interval `[γ − 90°, γ + 90°]`. -/
sig: theorem mem_angleIcc_of_cos_nonneg_single {γ β : ℝ} (h : 0 ≤ Real.cos (β - γ)) : β ∈ angleIcc (γ - π / 2) (γ + π / 2)

name: cos_nonneg_of_mem_coneAt
doc:
/-- **The tangent cone of a unit disc at a boundary point**: a set inside `B̄(y + e γ, 1)` approaches `y` only along directions
`β` with `cos(β − γ) ≥ 0`. -/
sig: theorem cos_nonneg_of_mem_coneAt {S : Set ℂ} {y : ℂ} {γ : ℝ} (hS : S ⊆ closedBall (y + e γ) 1) {β : ℝ} (hβ : β ∈ coneAt S y) : 0 ≤ Real.cos (β - γ)

name: flank_cone
doc:
/-- **FS116-Y4-FLANK**, the cones: let `t` be a tile with `y = r(ψ)` and `y' = r(ψ + 60°)` in its closure, its cone at `y`
containing `(ψ + 150°, ψ + 210°)` and its cone at `y'` containing `(ψ + 210°, ψ + 270°)`; then its cone at `y` lies in
`[ψ + 30°, ψ + 210°]` and holds `ψ + 210°` (it ends there), and its cone at `y'` lies in `[ψ + 210°, ψ + 390°]` and holds
`ψ + 210°` (it begins there). -/
sig: theorem flank_cone (hF : F.Valid) {t : Set ℂ} (ht : F.IsTile t) {p : ℂ} {ψ : ℝ} (hy : ringPt p ψ ∈ closure t) (hy' : ringPt p (ψ + π / 3) ∈ closure t) (hcy : Ioo (ψ + 5 * π / 6) (ψ + 7 * π / 6) ⊆ coneAt t (ringPt p ψ)) (hcy' : Ioo (ψ + 7 * π / 6) (ψ + 3 * π / 2) ⊆ coneAt t (ringPt p (ψ + π / 3))) : coneAt t (ringPt p ψ) ⊆ angleIcc (ψ + π / 6) (ψ + 7 * π / 6) ∧ ψ + 7 * π / 6 ∈ coneAt t (ringPt p ψ) ∧ coneAt t (ringPt p (ψ + π / 3)) ⊆ angleIcc (ψ + 7 * π / 6) (ψ + 13 * π / 6) ∧ ψ + 7 * π / 6 ∈ coneAt t (ringPt p (ψ + π / 3))

name: flank_edge_exists
doc:
/-- **FS116-Y4-FLANK**, the edges exist: at `y` (in the domain) under the cone hypotheses, `t`'s edge leaving `y` in the
direction `ψ + 210°` is an initial piece of an arc of the map lying in `cl t`; likewise at `y'`. -/
sig: theorem flank_edge_exists (hF : F.Valid) {t : Set ℂ} (ht : F.IsTile t) {p : ℂ} {ψ : ℝ} (hyd : ringPt p ψ ∈ F.dom) (hy'd : ringPt p (ψ + π / 3) ∈ F.dom) (hy : ringPt p ψ ∈ closure t) (hy' : ringPt p (ψ + π / 3) ∈ closure t) (hcy : Ioo (ψ + 5 * π / 6) (ψ + 7 * π / 6) ⊆ coneAt t (ringPt p ψ)) (hcy' : Ioo (ψ + 7 * π / 6) (ψ + 3 * π / 2) ⊆ coneAt t (ringPt p (ψ + π / 3))) : (∃ α ∈ F.arcs, ∃ B, α.InitialPiece (ringPt p ψ) (ψ + 7 * π / 6) B ∧ B ⊆ closure t) ∧ ∃ α' ∈ F.arcs, ∃ B', α'.InitialPiece (ringPt p (ψ + π / 3)) (ψ + 7 * π / 6) B' ∧ B' ⊆ closure t

name: e_sigma_half
sig: theorem e_sigma_half {σ : ℝ} (hσ : σ = 1 ∨ σ = -1) : e (σ * (π / 2)) = (σ : ℂ) * I

name: initialPiece_cases
doc:
/-- An initial piece of an arc leaving `y` in the direction `i m` (`‖m‖ = 1`): either the arc is a segment and the piece
contains `y + ε i m`, or it is circular and contains the points `y + σρ m (e(σt) − 1)`, `0 ≤ t ≤ ε`, `σ = ±1`. -/
sig: theorem initialPiece_cases {α : Arc} {y m : ℂ} {δ : ℝ} {B : Set ℂ} (hδ : e δ = I * m) (hB : α.InitialPiece y δ B) : (∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ y + (ε : ℂ) * (I * m) ∈ B) ∨ ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧ ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ∃ σ : ℝ, (σ = 1 ∨ σ = -1) ∧ ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 ε, y + ((σ * ρ : ℝ) : ℂ) * m * (e (σ * t) - 1) ∈ B

name: sq_norm_pieceB
doc: /-- The squared norm of `σρ(e(σt) − 1) − 1` (the offset of a point of a piece from the far point). -/
sig: theorem sq_norm_pieceB {σ ρ : ℝ} (hσ : σ = 1 ∨ σ = -1) (t : ℝ) : ‖((σ * ρ : ℝ) : ℂ) * (e (σ * t) - 1) - 1‖ ^ 2 = 1 + 2 * ρ * (ρ + σ) * (1 - Real.cos t)

name: sq_norm_pieceB'
doc: /-- The squared norm of `1 + σρ(e(σt) − 1)` (the offset of a point of a piece at the far end from the near point). -/
sig: theorem sq_norm_pieceB' {σ ρ : ℝ} (hσ : σ = 1 ∨ σ = -1) (t : ℝ) : ‖1 + ((σ * ρ : ℝ) : ℂ) * (e (σ * t) - 1)‖ ^ 2 = 1 + 2 * ρ * (ρ - σ) * (1 - Real.cos t)

name: flank_initialPieces
doc:
/-- **FS116-Y4-FLANK**, the geometry (TWOCIRC in place of its identity step, SR1 item 1): two initial pieces of arcs leaving
`y` and `y'` (with `y' − y = e(ψ + 120°)`) in the direction `ψ + 210°`, the first inside `B̄(y', 1)` and the second inside
`B̄(y, 1)`, have points nearer than `1`. (Staying in the disc forces each to curve toward the other centre with radius at most
`1`: a segment, or an arc
sig: theorem flank_initialPieces {y y' : ℂ} {ψ : ℝ} (hyy' : y' - y = e (ψ + 2 * π / 3)) {α α' : Arc} {B B' : Set ℂ} (hB : α.InitialPiece y (ψ + 7 * π / 6) B) (hB' : α'.InitialPiece y' (ψ + 7 * π / 6) B') (hBd : B ⊆ closedBall y' 1) (hB'd : B' ⊆ closedBall y 1) : ∃ z ∈ B, ∃ z' ∈ B', dist z z' < 1

name: flank
doc:
/-- **FS116-Y4-FLANK**, the row's last clause (for any sets `a`, `b` whose closures hold the two edges: the row's tiles
bordering `t` along them, or `t` itself): some point of `cl a` and some point of `cl b` are nearer than `1`. -/
sig: theorem flank (hF : F.Valid) {t : Set ℂ} (ht : F.IsTile t) {p : ℂ} {ψ : ℝ} (hy : ringPt p ψ ∈ closure t) (hy' : ringPt p (ψ + π / 3) ∈ closure t) {α α' : Arc} {B B' : Set ℂ} (hB : α.InitialPiece (ringPt p ψ) (ψ + 7 * π / 6) B) (hB' : α'.InitialPiece (ringPt p (ψ + π / 3)) (ψ + 7 * π / 6) B') (hBt : B ⊆ closure t) (hB't : B' ⊆ closure t) {a b : Set ℂ} (ha : B ⊆ closure a) (hb : B' ⊆ closure b) : ∃ z ∈ closure a, ∃ z' ∈ closure b, dist z z' < 1

name: sixSector
doc: /-- The sector index `⌊arg x / 60°⌋ mod 6`. -/
sig: noncomputable def sixSector (x : ℂ) : ZMod 6

name: sixRound
doc: /-- The nearest lens index `round(arg x / 60°)` (as an integer; the lens centres `e(60°m ± 30°)` depend on it mod 6). -/
sig: noncomputable def sixRound (x : ℂ) : ℤ

name: InSixLens
doc: /-- `x` lies in the open lens about the direction `60°m`: within `1` of `e(60°m − 30°)` and of `e(60°m + 30°)`. -/
sig: def InSixLens (m : ℤ) (x : ℂ) : Prop

name: sixCol
doc:
/-- The colour of FS116-Y2-SIXFRAG: sector index inside the unit disc; lens index `+ 2` in a lens; sector index `+ 4` in a
gap. -/
sig: noncomputable def sixCol (x : ℂ) : Fin 6

name: sixArcs
doc: /-- The arcs of FS116-Y2-SIXFRAG: six radial segments, the unit circle, twelve lens sides. -/
sig: noncomputable def sixArcs : Set Arc

name: sixArcs_nondegenerate
doc: /-- The arcs of `sixArcs` have positive length. -/
sig: theorem sixArcs_nondegenerate : ∀ a ∈ sixArcs, a.Nondegenerate

name: sixArcs_finite
doc: /-- `sixArcs` is finite. -/
sig: theorem sixArcs_finite : sixArcs.Finite

name: sixArcs_locallyFinite
doc: /-- Finitely many arcs: every point has a neighbourhood meeting finitely many. -/
sig: theorem sixArcs_locallyFinite : ∀ x ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) (3 / 2), ∃ t ∈ 𝓝 x, {a | a ∈ sixArcs ∧ (a.carrier ∩ t).Nonempty}.Finite

name: dist_polar_sq
doc: /-- The squared distance from the polar point `r e(φ)` to the unit-circle point `e(θ)`. -/
sig: theorem dist_polar_sq (r φ θ : ℝ) : dist ((r : ℂ) * e φ) (e θ) ^ 2 = r ^ 2 - 2 * r * Real.cos (φ - θ) + 1

name: arg_polar
doc: /-- The argument of a positive multiple of `e(φ)`, for `φ ∈ (−π, π]`. -/
sig: theorem arg_polar {r φ : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (hφ : φ ∈ Ioc (-π) π) : Complex.arg ((r : ℂ) * e φ) = φ

name: norm_polar
doc: /-- The norm of `r e(φ)`. -/
sig: theorem norm_polar {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (φ : ℝ) : ‖(r : ℂ) * e φ‖ = r

name: e_add_int_mul_two_pi
doc: /-- `e (θ + 2π k) = e θ` for an integer `k`. -/
sig: theorem e_add_int_mul_two_pi (θ : ℝ) (k : ℤ) : e (θ + k * (2 * π)) = e θ

name: inSixLens_add_six
doc: /-- The lens test is `6`-periodic in its index. -/
sig: theorem inSixLens_add_six (m k : ℤ) (x : ℂ) : InSixLens (m + 6 * k) x ↔ InSixLens m x

name: dist_polar_lt_one_iff
doc: /-- A point `r e(φ)`, `r > 0`, is within `1` of `e(α)` exactly when `r < 2 cos(φ − α)`. -/
sig: theorem dist_polar_lt_one_iff {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (φ α : ℝ) : dist ((r : ℂ) * e φ) (e α) < 1 ↔ r < 2 * Real.cos (φ - α)

name: dist_polar_eq_one_iff
doc: /-- A point `r e(φ)`, `r > 0`, is at distance exactly `1` from `e(α)` exactly when `r = 2 cos(φ − α)`. -/
sig: theorem dist_polar_eq_one_iff {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (φ α : ℝ) : dist ((r : ℂ) * e φ) (e α) = 1 ↔ r = 2 * Real.cos (φ - α)

name: eq_norm_mul_e_arg
doc: /-- A point `x ≠ 0` is `‖x‖ e(arg x)`. -/
sig: theorem eq_norm_mul_e_arg {x : ℂ} : x = (‖x‖ : ℂ) * e (Complex.arg x)

name: exists_int_abs_lt_of_half_lt_cos
doc: /-- If `1/2 < cos u`, then `u` is within `π/3` of a multiple of `2π`. -/
sig: theorem exists_int_abs_lt_of_half_lt_cos {u : ℝ} (h : 1 / 2 < Real.cos u) : ∃ k : ℤ, |u - k * (2 * π)| < π / 3

name: sixRound_of_lens
doc: /-- A lens point outside the open unit disc has round index congruent to the lens index. -/
sig: theorem sixRound_of_lens {x : ℂ} (hx : 1 ≤ ‖x‖) {m : ℤ} (h : InSixLens m x) : ∃ k : ℤ, sixRound x = m + 6 * k

name: sixCol_of_lens
doc: /-- A point outside the open unit disc inside a lens has the lens colour. -/
sig: theorem sixCol_of_lens {x : ℂ} (hx : 1 ≤ ‖x‖) {m : ℤ} (h : InSixLens m x) : sixCol x = (((m : ℤ) : ZMod 6) + 2 : ZMod 6)

name: e_pi_div_six
sig: theorem e_pi_div_six : e (π / 6) = ((Real.sqrt 3 / 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((1 / 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) * I

name: e_neg_pi_div_six
sig: theorem e_neg_pi_div_six : e (-(π / 6)) = ((Real.sqrt 3 / 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) - ((1 / 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) * I

name: re_nonneg_aux
doc: /-- Real arithmetic of the lens boundary: `a² + b² = 1`, `b ≥ 1/2` and `|(a + √3/2, b − 1/2)| ≥ 1` force `a ≥ 0`. -/
sig: theorem re_nonneg_aux (a b s : ℝ) (hs : s ^ 2 = 3) (hs0 : 0 < s) (hab : a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 = 1) (hb : 1 / 2 ≤ b) (h : 1 ≤ (a + s / 2) ^ 2 + (b - 1 / 2) ^ 2) : 0 ≤ a

name: lens_boundary_core
doc:
/-- The core of "a lens boundary point is on a lens side", in the frame of the lens `Q_0` (centres `e(∓30°)`): a point
outside the open unit disc, on the circle about `e(−30°)` and in the closed disc about `e(30°)`, is `e(−30°) + e(ψ)` with
`ψ ∈ [30°, 90°]`. -/
sig: theorem lens_boundary_core {x : ℂ} (hx : 1 ≤ ‖x‖) (h1 : dist x (e (-(π / 6))) = 1) (h2 : dist x (e (π / 6)) ≤ 1) : ∃ ψ ∈ Icc (π / 6) (π / 2), x = e (-(π / 6)) + e ψ

name: exists_fin_six_rep
doc: /-- Every integer multiple of `60°` is a multiple of `60°` in `{0, …, 5}` plus whole turns. -/
sig: theorem exists_fin_six_rep (m : ℤ) : ∃ (j : Fin 6) (n : ℤ), (m : ℝ) * (π / 3) = ((j : ℕ) : ℝ) * (π / 3) + n * (2 * π)

name: mem_arcs_side₁
doc: /-- The first family of lens-side points: `e(60°m − 30°) + e(ψ)` for `ψ ∈ [60°m + 30°, 60°m + 90°]` lies on `Γ`. -/
sig: theorem mem_arcs_side₁ (m : ℤ) {ψ : ℝ} (hψ : ψ ∈ Icc (m * (π / 3) + π / 6) (m * (π / 3) + π / 2)) : e (m * (π / 3) - π / 6) + e ψ ∈ ⋃ a ∈ sixArcs, a.carrier

name: mem_arcs_side₂
doc: /-- The second family of lens-side points: `e(60°m + 30°) + e(ψ)` for `ψ ∈ [60°m − 90°, 60°m − 30°]` lies on `Γ`. -/
sig: theorem mem_arcs_side₂ (m : ℤ) {ψ : ℝ} (hψ : ψ ∈ Icc (m * (π / 3) - π / 2) (m * (π / 3) - π / 6)) : e (m * (π / 3) + π / 6) + e ψ ∈ ⋃ a ∈ sixArcs, a.carrier

name: e_zero
sig: theorem e_zero : e 0 = 1

name: conj_e
doc: /-- The conjugate of `e θ` is `e (−θ)`. -/
sig: theorem conj_e (θ : ℝ) : (starRingEnd ℂ) (e θ) = e (-θ)

name: dist_rot
doc: /-- Rotating by `e(−60°m)` carries the lens `m` to the lens `0`. -/
sig: theorem dist_rot (x y : ℂ) (t : ℝ) : dist (x * e t) (y * e t) = dist x y

name: mem_arcs_of_lens_boundary₁
doc:
/-- **A lens boundary point is on a lens side (first family).** A point outside the open unit disc, on the circle about
`e(60°m − 30°)` and in the closed disc about `e(60°m + 30°)`, lies on a lens side of `sixArcs`. -/
sig: theorem mem_arcs_of_lens_boundary₁ {x : ℂ} (hx : 1 ≤ ‖x‖) (m : ℤ) (h1 : dist x (e (m * (π / 3) - π / 6)) = 1) (h2 : dist x (e (m * (π / 3) + π / 6)) ≤ 1) : x ∈ ⋃ a ∈ sixArcs, a.carrier

name: mem_arcs_of_lens_boundary₂
doc: /-- **A lens boundary point is on a lens side (second family).** -/
sig: theorem mem_arcs_of_lens_boundary₂ {x : ℂ} (hx : 1 ≤ ‖x‖) (m : ℤ) (h1 : dist x (e (m * (π / 3) + π / 6)) = 1) (h2 : dist x (e (m * (π / 3) - π / 6)) ≤ 1) : x ∈ ⋃ a ∈ sixArcs, a.carrier

name: mem_arcs_of_norm_eq_one
doc: /-- The unit circle lies in the arcs. -/
sig: theorem mem_arcs_of_norm_eq_one {x : ℂ} (hn : ‖x‖ = 1) : x ∈ ⋃ a ∈ sixArcs, a.carrier

name: mem_arcs_radial
doc: /-- The radial segments lie in the arcs. -/
sig: theorem mem_arcs_radial {t : ℝ} (ht0 : 0 ≤ t) (ht1 : t ≤ 1) (k : ℤ) : (t : ℂ) * e (k * (π / 3)) ∈ ⋃ a ∈ sixArcs, a.carrier

name: inSixLens_reduce
doc: /-- The lens test depends on the index mod `6`: every index is equivalent to one in `{0, …, 5}`. -/
sig: theorem inSixLens_reduce (m : ℤ) : ∃ j : Fin 6, ∀ y : ℂ, InSixLens m y ↔ InSixLens (((j : ℕ) : ℤ)) y

name: exists_one_lt_dist_of_not_lens
doc:
/-- No lens contains the point and no lens boundary point lies on `Γ`... a point outside the unit disc, not on `Γ`,
off every lens, is off the closure of every lens: some lens distance exceeds `1`. -/
sig: theorem exists_one_lt_dist_of_not_lens {x : ℂ} (hx : 1 ≤ ‖x‖) (hxΓ : x ∉ ⋃ a ∈ sixArcs, a.carrier) (m : ℤ) (hm : ¬ InSixLens m x) : 1 < dist x (e (m * (π / 3) - π / 6)) ∨ 1 < dist x (e (m * (π / 3) + π / 6))

name: eventually_floor_arg
doc: /-- The floor of `arg y / (π/3)` is locally constant at a non-integer value. -/
sig: theorem eventually_floor_arg {x : ℂ} (hsl : x ∈ Complex.slitPlane) (hnint : ∀ n : ℤ, Complex.arg x / (π / 3) ≠ n) : ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝 x, ⌊Complex.arg y / (π / 3)⌋ = ⌊Complex.arg x / (π / 3)⌋

name: sixCol_locallyConstant
doc:
/-- `sixCol` is locally constant off the arcs, inside `B(0, 3/2)`: the floor of `arg x / 60°` jumps only on the rays
`60°j`, which inside the disc are radial segments and outside lie in lenses (where the round is constant); the round
jumps only on the rays `60°j + 30°`, which outside the disc lie in gaps (where it is not read); `arg` jumps only on the
ray `180°`; the lens test changes only on the
sig: theorem sixCol_locallyConstant : ∀ x ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) (3 / 2), x ∉ ⋃ a ∈ sixArcs, a.carrier → ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝 x, sixCol y = sixCol x

name: sixFrag
doc:
/-- **FS116-Y2-SIXFRAG's fragment**: the six-coloured map of `B(0, 3/2)` by the unit sector flower, six lenses and six gap
tiles. -/
sig: noncomputable def sixFrag : ArcMap 6

doc: /-- The point `1/2` of the sector `S_0` has colour `0`. -/
sig: example : sixCol (1 / 2) = 0

doc: /-- The point `6/5` of the lens `Q_0` has colour `2`. -/
sig: example : sixCol (6 / 5) = 2

doc: /-- The point `(6/5) e(30°)` of the gap tile `G_0` has colour `4`. -/
sig: example : sixCol ((6 / 5 : ℂ) * e (π / 6)) = 4

doc: /-- The point `(1/2) e(210°)` of the sector `S_3` (an angle with negative `arg`) has colour `3`. -/
sig: example : sixCol ((1 / 2 : ℂ) * e (7 * π / 6)) = 3

name: norm_e_add_e_sq
sig: theorem norm_e_add_e_sq (a b : ℝ) : ‖e a + e b‖ ^ 2 = 2 + 2 * Real.cos (a - b)

name: one_le_norm_e_add_e
doc:
/-- Points of the two lens-side families (angle difference at least `60°` and at most `120°` in absolute value) are at
distance at least `1` from `0`: `‖e a + e b‖² = 2 + 2 cos(a − b) ≥ 1` once `|a − b| ≤ 120°`. -/
sig: theorem one_le_norm_e_add_e {a b : ℝ} (h2 : |b - a| ≤ 2 * π / 3) : 1 ≤ ‖e a + e b‖

name: sixFrag_mem_interiorPts
doc: /-- A point of the open sector `(60°j, 60°(j+1))` of the open unit disc is an interior point of `sixFrag`. -/
sig: theorem sixFrag_mem_interiorPts {t φ : ℝ} {j : ℤ} (ht : 0 < t) (ht1 : t < 1) (hφ1 : j * (π / 3) < φ) (hφ2 : φ < (j + 1) * (π / 3)) : (t : ℂ) * e φ ∈ sixFrag.interiorPts

name: sixCol_sector
doc: /-- The colour of a point of the open sector `(60°j, 60°(j+1))` of the open unit disc, `−3 ≤ j ≤ 2`, is `j`. -/
sig: theorem sixCol_sector {t φ : ℝ} {j : ℤ} (ht : 0 < t) (ht1 : t < 1) (hj1 : -3 ≤ j) (hj2 : j ≤ 2) (hφ1 : j * (π / 3) < φ) (hφ2 : φ < (j + 1) * (π / 3)) : sixCol ((t : ℂ) * e φ) = ((j : ℤ) : ZMod 6)

name: zero_mem_closure_region
doc: /-- Each colour `c` is carried at `0`: the open sector of colour `c` approaches `0`. -/
sig: theorem zero_mem_closure_region {j : ℤ} (hj1 : -3 ≤ j) (hj2 : j ≤ 2) : (0 : ℂ) ∈ closure (sixFrag.region ((j : ℤ) : ZMod 6))

name: e_ne_zero'
sig: theorem e_ne_zero' (θ : ℝ) : e θ ≠ 0

name: dist_rot_left
doc: /-- Left multiplication by `a` scales distances by `‖a‖`. -/
sig: theorem dist_rot_left (a x y : ℂ) : dist (a * x) (a * y) = ‖a‖ * dist x y

name: exists_int_of_e_eq_e
doc: /-- `e a = e b` forces `a = b + 2π n`. -/
sig: theorem exists_int_of_e_eq_e {a b : ℝ} (h : e a = e b) : ∃ n : ℤ, a = b + n * (2 * π)

name: arg_rot
doc: /-- Rotating by `60° k` moves the argument by `60° k` plus whole turns. -/
sig: theorem arg_rot {x : ℂ} (hx : x ≠ 0) (k : ℤ) : ∃ n : ℤ, Complex.arg (e (k * (π / 3)) * x) = Complex.arg x + k * (π / 3) + n * (2 * π)

name: inSixLens_rot
doc: /-- The lens test rotates with the index. -/
sig: theorem inSixLens_rot (k m : ℤ) (x : ℂ) : InSixLens (m + k) (e (k * (π / 3)) * x) ↔ InSixLens m x

name: sixCol_rot
doc: /-- **Rotation by `60° k` adds `k` to the colour.** -/
sig: theorem sixCol_rot (k : ℤ) {x : ℂ} (hx : x ≠ 0) : sixCol (e (k * (π / 3)) * x) = ((show ZMod 6 from sixCol x) + ((k : ℤ) : ZMod 6) : ZMod 6)

name: sixFrag_valid
doc:
/-- **FS116-Y2-SIXFRAG**, validity: no two interior points of one colour are at distance exactly `1`. Colour `0` (and every
other, by the rotation by `60°`) is carried by `S_0`, `Q_4`, `G_2`: three diameters below `1`, three cross distances above
`1`, exact in `ℚ(√3, √7)` (the cut points of the lenses have cosine `3/4`). -/
sig: theorem sixFrag_valid : sixFrag.Valid

name: sixFrag_nonSiamese
doc:
/-- **FS116-Y2-SIXFRAG**, non-Siamese: two distinct tiles of one colour always have a pair of points at distance at least
`1`. -/
sig: theorem sixFrag_nonSiamese : sixFrag.NonSiamese

name: sixFrag_covers
doc: /-- **FS116-Y2-SIXFRAG**, the disc: the fragment holds `B̄(0, R)` for every `R < 3/2`. -/
sig: theorem sixFrag_covers {R : ℝ} (hR : R < 3 / 2) : sixFrag.Covers 0 R

name: sixFrag_coloursAt_zero
doc: /-- **FS116-Y2-SIXFRAG**, the vertex: all six colours are carried at `0`. -/
sig: theorem sixFrag_coloursAt_zero : sixFrag.coloursAt 0 = univ

name: sixFrag_sphere_subset_Γ
doc: /-- **FS116-Y2-SIXFRAG**, the ring lies in `Γ`. -/

name: norm_e_sub_e_sq
sig: theorem norm_e_sub_e_sq (a b : ℝ) : ‖e a - e b‖ ^ 2 = 2 - 2 * Real.cos (a - b)

name: no_int_lens

sig: theorem no_int_lens {θ : ℝ} (h0 : 0 < θ) (h1 : θ < π / 6) {N : ℤ} (hθ : θ = π / 6 + N * (π / 3)) : False

name: no_int_radial
doc: /-- No integer `N` has `0 < N·60°/... `: `θ = N·(π/3)` with `0 < θ < π/6` is impossible. -/
sig: theorem no_int_radial {θ : ℝ} (h0 : 0 < θ) (h1 : θ < π / 6) {N : ℤ} (hθ : θ = N * (π / 3)) : False

name: norm_e_sub_lens_ne
doc:
/-- A point `e θ` of the ring strictly between `0°` and `30°` is not at distance `1` from any lens centre
`e(30° + 60°m)`. -/
sig: theorem norm_e_sub_lens_ne {θ : ℝ} (h0 : 0 < θ) (h1 : θ < π / 6) (m : ℤ) : ‖e θ - e (π / 6 + m * (π / 3))‖ ≠ 1

name: sin_eq_zero_of_mem_radial
doc: /-- A point `t e(φ)`, `t > 0`, on the radial segment towards `e(60°k)` has `sin(φ − 60°k) = 0`. -/
sig: theorem sin_eq_zero_of_mem_radial {t φ : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) {k : ℕ} (h : (t : ℂ) * e φ ∈ segment ℝ 0 (e (k * (π / 3)))) : Real.sin (φ - k * (π / 3)) = 0

name: e_notMem_lens_union
doc: /-- The ring point `e θ`, `0 < θ < 30°`, is on no radial segment and no lens side. -/
sig: theorem e_notMem_lens_union {θ : ℝ} (h0 : 0 < θ) (h1 : θ < π / 6) : e θ ∉ ⋃ a ∈ {a | a ∈ sixArcs ∧ a ≠ Arc.circ 0 1 0 (2 * π)}, a.carrier

name: dist_polar_same

name: sixCol_inner_zero
doc: /-- Inside the unit disc, an argument in `(0°, 60°)` means colour `0`. -/
sig: theorem sixCol_inner_zero {z : ℂ} (hz : ‖z‖ < 1) (ha : Complex.arg z ∈ Ioo 0 (π / 3)) : sixCol z = 0

name: sixCol_outer_two
doc: /-- Outside the unit disc, an argument in `(0°, 30°)` and the two lens tests mean colour `2`. -/
sig: theorem sixCol_outer_two {z : ℂ} (hz : 1 ≤ ‖z‖) (ha : Complex.arg z ∈ Ioo 0 (π / 6)) (l1 : dist z (e (-(π / 6))) < 1) (l2 : dist z (e (π / 6)) < 1) : sixCol z = 2

name: sixFrag_isQArc
doc: /-- **FS116-Y2-SIXFRAG**, every arc of `Γ` on `ω(0)` (with constant sides) is a (Q) arc. -/

sig: theorem sixFrag_isRingArc : sixFrag.IsRingArc 0 0 (π / 6) 0 2

name: ne1_region
doc:

sig: theorem ne1_region (hF : F.Valid) {c : Fin k} {x z : ℂ} (hx : x ∈ closure (F.region c)) (hz : z ∈ F.region c) : dist z x ≠ 1

doc:

class of `c` and any preconnected `S` inside the closure of the class, every point of `S` is nearer than `1` to `z`, or

doc:

tile of colour `c`; if some point of the union is nearer than `1` to some point of `cl U`, every point of the union is
within `1` of every point of `cl U`. -/
sig: theorem cluster (hF : F.Valid) {c : Fin k} {𝒯 : Set (Set ℂ)} (hfin : 𝒯.Finite) (h𝒯 : ∀ T ∈ 𝒯, F.TileOf c T) (hconn : IsPreconnected (⋃ T ∈ 𝒯, closure T)) {U : Set ℂ} (hU : F.TileOf c U) (hnear : ∃ x ∈ ⋃ T ∈ 𝒯, closure T, ∃ y ∈ closure U, dist x y < 1) : ∀ x ∈ ⋃ T ∈ 𝒯, closure T, ∀ y ∈ closure U, dist x y ≤ 1

doc:

name: not_mem_closure_wholeRestrict_of_inner
doc:
/-- **FS129-OR1-WHOLE**, the `R₂` clause, at the class its argument reads (pointwise in the arc, and with no use of the
arc lying in `Γ`): for `ρ ≤ √3`, if `p + e θ` is a closure point of the part inside `B(p, 1)` of a tile `T` of colour `c`
of `F`, no tile of `F_ρ` of colour `c` has `p + 2 e θ` in its closure. (A tile of `F_ρ` of colour `c` lies in
`B(p + 2e θ, 1)` and meets `B(p, √3)`, so by the

name: not_mem_closure_wholeRestrict_R₂
doc:
/-- **FS129-OR1-WHOLE**, the `R₂` clause in the row's form: for `ρ ≤ √3` and an arc `r([θ₁, θ₂])` of `ω(p)` of positive

sig: theorem not_mem_closure_wholeRestrict_R₂ {p : ℂ} {ρ : ℝ} (hF : F.Valid) (hρ : ρ ≤ √3) {c : Fin k} {T : Set ℂ} (hT : F.TileOf c T) {θ₁ θ₂ : ℝ} (h12 : θ₁ < θ₂) (hinner : ∀ θ ∈ Ioo θ₁ θ₂, ∃ δ > 0, ∀ η ∈ Ioo 0 δ, p + ((1 - η : ℝ) : ℂ) * e θ ∈ T) {T' : Set ℂ} (hT' : (F.wholeRestrict p ρ).TileOf c T') : ∀ θ ∈ Icc θ₁ θ₂, p + 2 * e θ ∉ closure T'
